sentences.zh: 泥婆羅國泥婆羅國，在吐蕃西。

translations.literal: The country of Nipolo—Nipolo lies to the west of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Nepal lies west of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 其俗翦髮與眉齊，穿耳，揎以竹桶牛角，綴至肩者以為姣麗。

translations.literal: Their custom is to cut the hair level with the eyebrows and pierce the ears; they enlarge them with bamboo tubes and ox horns, and those adorned down to the shoulders are considered beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they crop their hair to the brow line and pierce their ears, stretching the lobes with bamboo tubes and ox horns; ornaments that hang to the shoulders are regarded as the height of beauty.

sentences.zh: 食用手，無匕箸。

translations.literal: They eat with their hands and have no spoons or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They eat with their hands and use neither spoons nor chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 其器皆銅。

translations.literal: Their vessels are all of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: All their utensils are made of bronze.

sentences.zh: 多商賈，少田作。

translations.literal: There are many merchants and few who work the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants abound, while farming is scarce.

sentences.zh: 以銅為錢，面文為人，背文為馬牛，不穿孔。

translations.literal: They use bronze for coinage; the obverse bears the image of a man, the reverse that of horses and cattle, and they are not pierced.
translations.idiomatic: Their currency is bronze coins bearing a human face on one side and horses and cattle on the other, without a central hole.

sentences.zh: 衣服以一幅蔽布身，日數盥浴。

translations.literal: For clothing they use a single breadth of cloth to cover the body, and they bathe several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: They dress in a single length of cloth wrapped about the body and wash themselves several times daily.

sentences.zh: 以板為屋，壁皆雕畫。

translations.literal: They build houses of planks, and the walls are all carved and painted.
translations.idiomatic: Their houses are of timber, and every wall is carved and painted.

sentences.zh: 俗重博戲，好吹蠡擊鼓。

translations.literal: The people greatly esteem gambling games and delight in playing reed pipes and beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: They are fond of games of chance and love to play reed flutes and beat drums.

sentences.zh: 頗解推測盈虛，兼通曆術。

translations.literal: They are quite skilled at calculating surplus and deficit and are also versed in calendrical arts.
translations.idiomatic: They are fairly adept at astronomical calculation and understand calendrical science as well.

sentences.zh: 事五天神，鐫石為像，每日清水浴神，烹羊而祭。

translations.literal: They serve the Five Heavenly Deities, carving stone into images; each day they bathe the gods with clear water and cook sheep as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They worship the Five Heavenly Deities, carving their images in stone, bathing the idols daily with fresh water, and sacrificing cooked sheep.

sentences.zh: 其王那陵提婆，身著真珠、玻璃、車渠、珊瑚、琥珀、瓔珞，耳垂金鉤玉榼，佩寶裝伏突，坐獅子床，其堂內散花燃香。

translations.literal: Their king Narendradeva wore pearls, glass, conch shell, coral, amber, and strings of beads; from his earlobes hung gold hooks and jade cups; he wore jeweled boots; he sat on a lion couch; within his hall flowers were scattered and incense burned.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Narendradeva was arrayed in pearls, crystal, conch, coral, amber, and jeweled necklaces; gold hooks and jade vessels hung from his ears; he wore gem-studded boots and sat upon a lion throne while flowers were strewn and incense burned in his hall.

sentences.zh: 大臣及諸左右並坐於地，持兵數百列侍其側。

translations.literal: Ministers and all those at his side likewise sat on the ground, while several hundred men bearing weapons stood in ranks at his flanks.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers and attendants all sat on the floor, while hundreds of armed guards lined both sides of him.

sentences.zh: 宮中有七層之樓，覆以銅瓦，欄檻楹栿皆飾珠寶。

translations.literal: Within the palace was a seven-story tower roofed with bronze tiles; railings, balustrades, pillars, and beams were all adorned with pearls and gems.
translations.idiomatic: The palace contained a seven-tiered tower roofed in bronze tiles, its railings, pillars, and beams all set with pearls and precious stones.

sentences.zh: 樓之四角，各懸銅槽，下有金龍，激水上樓，註於槽中，從龍口而出，狀若飛泉。

translations.literal: At each corner of the tower hung a bronze trough; below were golden dragons that pumped water up the tower into the troughs, whence it issued from the dragons' mouths like flying springs.
translations.idiomatic: At each corner of the tower hung a bronze channel; golden dragons below forced water up into the channels, and it poured from their mouths like cascading fountains.

sentences.zh: 那陵提婆之父，為其叔父所篡，那陵提婆逃難於外，吐蕃因而納焉，克復其位，遂羈屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Narendradeva's father was usurped by his uncle; Narendradeva fled into exile abroad, whereupon Tibet received him, helped him recover his throne, and he thus became bound to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Narendradeva's father had been overthrown by an uncle; Narendradeva fled into exile, and Tibet took him in, restored him to his throne, after which Nepal became a Tibetan dependency.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，衛尉丞李義表往使天竺，塗經其國，那陵提婆見之，大喜，與義表同出觀阿耆婆沴池。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan reign, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Yibiao was sent on a mission to India and passed through their country on the way; Narendradeva saw him and was greatly pleased, and together with Yibiao went out to view the Ajiaposhi hot spring.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Li Yibiao traveled to India and passed through Nepal en route; Narendradeva was delighted to meet him and went out with Yibiao to see the Ajiaposhi hot springs.

sentences.zh: 周回二十餘步，水恆沸，雖流潦暴集，爍石焦金，未嘗增減。

translations.literal: Its circumference was a little over twenty paces; the water was perpetually boiling, and though torrents might suddenly gather or stones be heated to glow and metal scorched, it never increased or decreased.
translations.idiomatic: The pool measured a little over twenty paces around; the water boiled constantly, and though floods might rush in or stones be heated white-hot, its level never rose or fell.

sentences.zh: 以物投之，即生煙焰，懸釜而炊，須臾而熟。

translations.literal: If one cast something into it, smoke and flame at once arose; suspend a cauldron over it and food was cooked in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Anything thrown in immediately burst into smoke and flame; hung with a pot, it would cook food in moments.

sentences.zh: 其後王玄策為天竺所掠，泥婆羅發騎與吐蕃共破天竺有功，

translations.literal: Later Wang Xuance was captured by India; Nipolo sent horsemen and, together with Tibet, broke India and rendered meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Xuance was seized in India, Nepal sent cavalry and, together with Tibet, defeated the Indians—a deed of great merit.

sentences.zh: 其王屍利那連陀羅又遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, their king Shilinaliantuoluo again sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui (651), King Shilinaliantuoluo again dispatched envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 党項羌党項羌，在古析支之地，漢西羌之別種也。

translations.literal: The Tangut Qiang—the Tangut Qiang dwell in the ancient land of Qizhi and are a separate branch of the Western Qiang of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut Qiang inhabit the ancient territory of Qizhi and are a distinct offshoot of the Western Qiang known to the Han.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之後，西羌微弱，或臣中國，或竄山野。

translations.literal: After the Wei and Jin dynasties the Western Qiang grew weak; some submitted to China, others fled into mountains and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Jin periods the Western Qiang declined; some tribes submitted to China, while others took refuge in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 自周氏滅宕昌、鄧至之後，党項始強。

translations.literal: From the time the Zhou house destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi, the Tangut began to grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Northern Zhou destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi, the Tangut began to rise in power.

sentences.zh: 其界東至松州，西接葉護，南雜舂桑、迷桑等羌，北連吐谷渾，處山谷間，互三千里。

translations.literal: Their borders reached east to Songzhou, west joined Yehu, south mingled with the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang, north connected with Tuyuhun; they dwelt among valleys and ravines across three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory extended east to Songzhou, west to the Yehu lands, south among the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang peoples, and north to Tuyuhun—some three thousand li of mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 其種每姓別自為部落，一姓之中復分為小部落，大者萬餘騎，小者數千騎，不相統一。

translations.literal: Each clan surname formed its own tribe; within one surname they were further divided into lesser tribes—the large had more than ten thousand horsemen, the small several thousand, and they were not unified under one rule.
translations.idiomatic: Each surname formed its own tribe, and within each surname were smaller sub-tribes—large ones fielded over ten thousand horsemen, small ones a few thousand, with no single authority over all.

sentences.zh: 有細封氏、費聽氏、往利氏、頗超氏、野辭氏、房當氏、米擒氏、拓拔氏，而拓拔最為強族。

translations.literal: There were the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans, of whom the Tuoba were the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans, the Tuoba being the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 俗皆土著，居有棟宇，其屋織牦牛尾及羊毛覆之，每年一易。

translations.literal: By custom they were all settled inhabitants; their dwellings had frames, and their houses were thatched with woven yak tails and wool, replaced every year.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary by custom, living in framed houses roofed with woven yak tails and wool, renewed each year.

sentences.zh: 俗尚武，無法令賦役。

translations.literal: They esteemed martial valor and had no statutes, taxes, or corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: They valued martial prowess and knew neither written law nor regular taxation.

sentences.zh: 其人多壽，年一百五六十歲。

translations.literal: Their people were mostly long-lived, reaching one hundred fifty or sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Many lived to a great age, often a hundred and fifty or sixty years.

sentences.zh: 不事產業，好為盜竊，互相淩劫。

translations.literal: They did not engage in productive work but delighted in theft and plundered one another.
translations.idiomatic: They did not pursue honest livelihoods but delighted in raiding and robbing one another.

sentences.zh: 尤重復仇，若仇人未得，必蓬頭垢面跣足蔬食，要斬仇人而後復常。

translations.literal: They especially valued vengeance; if the enemy had not been taken, they would go with disheveled hair, filthy faces, bare feet, and plain food, resolved to behead the foe before returning to normal life.
translations.idiomatic: Blood vengeance mattered above all: until the enemy was slain, they went unkempt, barefoot, and abstemious, vowing not to resume ordinary life until the killer was dead.

sentences.zh: 男女並衣裘褐，仍被大氈。

translations.literal: Men and women alike wore fur and coarse cloth and still wrapped themselves in great felts.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike wore furs and coarse woolens, wrapped additionally in heavy felt cloaks.

sentences.zh: 畜牦牛、馬、驢、羊，以供其食。

translations.literal: They raised yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep to supply their food.
translations.idiomatic: They kept yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep for their sustenance.

sentences.zh: 不知稼穡，土無五谷。

translations.literal: They did not know grain cultivation, and their soil had none of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: They did not practice agriculture, for their land yielded none of the staple grains.

sentences.zh: 氣候多風寒，五月草始生，八月霜雪降。

translations.literal: The climate was mostly windy and cold; grass did not sprout until the fifth month, and frost and snow fell in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was harsh and cold; grass appeared only in the fifth month, and frost and snow came in the eighth.

sentences.zh: 求大麥於他界，醖以為酒。

translations.literal: They sought barley from other regions and fermented it into wine.
translations.idiomatic: They obtained barley from neighboring lands and brewed it into wine.

sentences.zh: 妻其庶母及伯叔母、嫂、子弟之婦，淫穢烝褻，諸夷中最為甚，然不婚同姓。

translations.literal: They took their stepmothers, paternal uncles' wives, sisters-in-law, and younger kinsmen's wives in marriage—licentious and incestuous beyond all other barbarians, yet they did not marry within the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: They married stepmothers, uncles' wives, sisters-in-law, and younger relatives' wives—more debauched in this respect than any other frontier people, though they would not marry within the same clan name.

sentences.zh: 老死者以為盡天年，親戚不哭；

translations.literal: When the aged died they considered it the completion of heaven's years, and kin did not weep;
translations.idiomatic: When the elderly died of natural causes, kin took it as a full lifespan and did not mourn;

sentences.zh: 少死者則雲夭枉，乃悲哭之。

translations.literal: when the young died they said it was an untimely death, and then they wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: but when the young died they called it an untimely end and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 死則焚屍，名為火葬。

translations.literal: Upon death they burned the corpse, called fire burial.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated in what they called fire burial.

sentences.zh: 無文字，但候草木以記歲時。

translations.literal: They had no writing but merely observed plants and trees to mark the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written language and reckoned the seasons only by watching when plants bloomed or withered.

sentences.zh: 三年一相聚，殺牛羊以祭天。

translations.literal: Once every three years they gathered together and slaughtered cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they assembled to slaughter cattle and sheep in sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自周及隋，或叛或朝，常為邊患，

translations.literal: From the Zhou through the Sui they sometimes rebelled and sometimes came to court, and were constantly a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou through the Sui they alternately rebelled and submitted, and were a perennial frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 南會州都督鄭元璹遣使招諭，其酋長細封步賴舉部內附，太宗降璽書慰撫之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, Regional Commander of South Huizhou Zheng Yuanshu sent envoys to summon and instruct them; the chieftain Xifeng Bulai led his tribe to submit inwardly, and Taizong issued an imperial edict to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629), Zheng Yuanshu, regional commander of South Huizhou, sent envoys to win them over; chieftain Xifeng Bulai brought his tribe to submit, and Emperor Taizong sent a sealed edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 步賴因來朝，宴賜甚厚，列其地為軌州，拜步賴為刺史。

translations.literal: Bulai thereupon came to court; he was feasted and rewarded very generously, his territory was established as Guizhou, and Bulai was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Bulai then came to court, was lavishly entertained and rewarded, his lands were organized as Guizhou, and he was appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 仍請率所部討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He further requested to lead his followers to campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to lead his people against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 其後諸姓酋長相次率部落皆來內屬。

translations.literal: Afterward chieftains of the various surnames in succession led their tribes to come and submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter chieftains of the other clans brought their tribes to submit one after another.

sentences.zh: 請同編戶，太宗厚加撫慰，列其地為崌、奉、巖、遠四州，各拜其首領為刺史。

translations.literal: They requested to be registered like ordinary households; Taizong greatly comforted and reassured them, established their lands as the four prefectures of Gui, Feng, Yan, and Yuan, and appointed each chieftain prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to be registered as ordinary subjects; Taizong treated them generously, organized their territory into the four prefectures of Gui, Feng, Yan, and Yuan, and appointed each chieftain as prefect.

sentences.zh: 有羌酋拓拔赤辭者，初臣屬吐谷渾，甚為渾主伏允所暱，與之結婚。

translations.literal: There was a Qiang chieftain Tuoba Chici who at first submitted to Tuyuhun and was greatly favored by the Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun, who gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: One Qiang leader, Tuoba Chici, had initially served Tuyuhun and was greatly favored by King Fuyun, who married him to a royal daughter.

sentences.zh: 及貞觀初，諸羌歸附，而赤辭不至。

translations.literal: When at the beginning of Zhenguan the various Qiang submitted, Chici did not come.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhenguan era, when the other Qiang submitted, Chici did not appear.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾，赤辭屯狼道坡以抗官軍。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, Chici encamped at Langdao Slope to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing campaigned against Tuyuhun, Chici held Langdao Slope to block the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 廓州刺史久且洛生遣使諭以禍福，赤辭曰：「我被渾主親戚之恩，腹心相寄，生死不貳，焉知其他。

translations.literal: Guozhou Prefect Jiujie Luosheng sent an envoy to explain fortune and disaster; Chici said, "I have received the Tuyuhun ruler's kindness as a kinsman; he entrusted me with his innermost affairs—I shall not be disloyal in life or death; how should I know anything else?
translations.idiomatic: Guozhou Prefect Jiujie Luosheng sent an envoy to warn him of the consequences; Chici replied, "The Tuyuhun king treated me as kin and trusted me with his innermost affairs. I shall be loyal unto death. What else is there to discuss?

sentences.zh: 汝可速去，無令汙我刀也。」

translations.literal: You may go quickly—do not let my blade be stained by you.
translations.idiomatic: Be off at once, lest you stain my blade.

sentences.zh: 洛生知其不悟，於是率輕騎襲之，擊破赤辭於肅遠山，斬首數百級，虜雜畜六千而還。

translations.literal: Luosheng knew he would not come to his senses; thereupon he led light cavalry in a surprise attack, defeated Chici at Mount Suyuan, beheaded several hundred, captured six thousand mixed livestock, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Chici would not listen, Luosheng led light cavalry in a surprise attack, routed him at Mount Suyuan, took several hundred heads, seized six thousand head of livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太宗又令岷州都督李道彥說諭之，赤辭從子思頭密送誠款，其黨拓拔細豆又以所部來降。

translations.literal: Taizong again ordered Minzhou Regional Commander Li Daoyan to persuade him; Chici's nephew Sitou secretly sent pledges of loyalty, and his follower Tuoba Xidou also came with his following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then sent Minzhou commander Li Daoyan to negotiate; Chici's nephew Sitou secretly pledged allegiance, and his follower Tuoba Xidou brought his band to surrender.

sentences.zh: 赤辭見其宗黨離，始有歸化之意。

translations.literal: Chici, seeing his clan and followers depart, first conceived the intention to submit and be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chici saw his kin and followers deserting him, he at last considered submission.

sentences.zh: 後岷州都督劉師立復遣人招誘，於是與思頭並率眾內屬，拜赤辭為西戎州都督，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: Later Minzhou Regional Commander Liu Shili again sent men to summon and entice him; thereupon he and Sitou together led the masses to submit inwardly; Chici was appointed Regional Commander of Xirongzhou and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Shili of Minzhou sent envoys again; Chici and Sitou then led their people to submit, and Chici was appointed regional commander of Xirongzhou and given the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 自此職貢不絕。

translations.literal: From this time tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃強盛，拓拔氏漸為所逼，遂請內徙，始移其部落於慶州，置靜邊等州以處之。

translations.literal: Later Tibet grew powerful and the Tuoba clan was gradually pressed by them; they therefore requested relocation inward and first moved their tribes to Qingzhou, establishing Jingbian and other prefectures to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: As Tibet grew powerful, the Tuoba were increasingly pressured and asked to move inward; their tribes were first resettled in Qingzhou, with Jingbian and other prefectures established to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其故地陷於吐蕃，其處者為其役屬，吐蕃謂之「弭藥」。

translations.literal: Their former lands fell to Tibet; those who remained there became its subjects and servants, and Tibet called them "Miyao."
translations.idiomatic: Their former homeland fell to Tibet; those who stayed behind became Tibetan subjects, whom the Tibetans called the Miyao.

sentences.zh: 又有黑党項，在於赤水之西。

translations.literal: There were also the Black Tangut, who dwelt west of the Red River.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Black Tangut, living west of the Red River.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾也，渾主伏允奔黑党項，居以空閑之地。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, the Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun fled to the Black Tangut, who gave him vacant lands to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, King Fuyun fled to the Black Tangut, who settled him on vacant pasturelands.

sentences.zh: 及吐谷渾舉國內屬，黑党項酋長號敦善王因貢方物。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun submitted with the whole state, the Black Tangut chieftain titled Dunshanwang thereupon presented local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun submitted en masse, the Black Tangut chieftain known as King Dunshan sent tribute of local goods.

sentences.zh: 又有雪山党項，姓破醜氏，居於雪山之下，及白狗、舂桑、白蘭等諸羌，自龍朔已後，並為吐蕃所破而臣屬焉。

translations.literal: There were also the Snow Mountain Tangut of the Pochou clan, dwelling below the snow mountains, and the Baigou, Chunsang, Bailan, and other Qiang—all from Longshuo onward were broken by Tibet and became its subjects.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Snow Mountain Tangut of the Pochou clan and the Baigou, Chunsang, Bailan, and other Qiang tribes; from the Longshuo era onward, all were defeated by Tibet and brought under its rule.

sentences.zh: 其在西北邊者，內附，凡二十萬口，分其地置朝、吳、浮、歸等十州，仍散居靈、夏等界內。

translations.literal: Those on the northwestern border who submitted inwardly numbered two hundred thousand persons in all; their lands were divided and ten prefectures established—Chao, Wu, Fu, Gui, and others—and they were still scattered to dwell within the boundaries of Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the northwest frontier who submitted numbered two hundred thousand souls; their territory was divided into ten prefectures including Chao, Wu, Fu, and Gui, and they were settled scattered within the Ling and Xia regions.

sentences.zh: 自至德已後，常為吐蕃所誘，密以官告授之，使為偵道，故時或侵叛，尋亦底寧。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward they were often enticed by Tibet, which secretly granted them official patents and made them scouts on the routes; hence they sometimes raided and rebelled, but soon settled again.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era they were often lured by Tibet, which secretly issued them official commissions as spies, so they sometimes raided or rebelled, though calm was usually restored before long.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，其首領來朝，請助國供靈州軍糧，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying their chieftains came to court and requested to aid the state by supplying grain for the Lingzhou army; an excellent edict praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying era their leaders came to court offering to supply grain for the Lingzhou garrison; the emperor issued a commendatory edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 其在涇、隴州界者，率其眾十餘萬，詣鳳翔節度使崔光遠請降。

translations.literal: Those within the borders of Jing and Long prefectures led their masses, more than a hundred thousand, to Fengxiang Military Commissioner Cui Guangyuan to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the Jing and Long region, numbering over a hundred thousand, went to Fengxiang commissioner Cui Guangyuan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二月，其歸順州部落、乾封州部落、歸義州部落、順化州部落、和寧州部落、和義州部落、保善州部落、寧定州部落、羅雲州部落、朝鳳州部落，並詣山南西道都防禦使、梁州刺史臧希讓請州印。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the tribes of Guishunzhou, Qianfengzhou, Guiyizhou, Shunhuazhou, He'ningzhou, Heyizhou, Baoshanzhou, Ningdingzhou, Luoyunzhou, and Chaofengzhou all went to the Defender-in-Chief of Southwestern Shannan Circuit and Liangzhou Prefect Zang Xirang to request prefectural seals.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the tribes of Guishun, Qianfeng, Guiyi, Shunhua, He'ning, Heyi, Baoshan, Ningding, Luoyun, and Chaofeng all went to Zang Xirang, defender of southwestern Shannan and prefect of Liangzhou, to request official prefectural seals.

sentences.zh: 希讓以聞，許之。

translations.literal: Xirang reported this and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xirang reported this to the throne, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，初禁商賈以牛、馬、器械於党項部落貿易。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, for the first time merchants were forbidden to trade cattle, horses, and weapons with Tangut tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a ban was first imposed on merchants trading cattle, horses, and weapons with Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，六州党項自石州奔過河西。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the six-prefecture Tangut fled from Shizhou across the river west of the He.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the six-prefecture Tangut fled from Shizhou across the Yellow River to the west.

sentences.zh: 党項有六府部落，曰野利越詩、野利龍兒、野利厥律、兒黃、野海、野窣等。

translations.literal: The Tangut had six-fu tribes called Yeliyueshi, Yelilong'er, Yelijuelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut comprised six fu tribes: Yeliyueshi, Yelilong'er, Yelijuelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and the like.

sentences.zh: 居慶州者號為東山部落，居夏州者號為平夏部落。

translations.literal: Those dwelling in Qingzhou were called the Eastern Mountain tribes; those in Xiazhou were called the Pingxia tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Those in Qingzhou were known as the Eastern Mountain tribes; those in Xiazhou as the Pingxia tribes.

sentences.zh: 永泰、大歷已後，居石州，依水草。

translations.literal: After Yongtai and Dali they dwelt in Shizhou, following water and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongtai and Dali eras they lived in Shizhou, following pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 至是永安城鎮將阿史那思昧擾其部落，求取駝馬無厭，中使又贊成其事，党項不堪其弊，遂率部落奔過河。

translations.literal: At this time Yong'an Fort garrison commander Ashina Simo harassed their tribes, demanding camels and horses without end; palace envoys moreover abetted the affair, and the Tangut could not bear the abuse; they therefore led their tribes in flight across the river.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yong'an garrison commander Ashina Simo was harassing them, demanding camels and horses without limit, abetted by court eunuchs; unable to endure the exactions, the Tangut led their tribes across the river.

sentences.zh: 五月，復置宥州以護党項。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Youzhou was re-established to protect the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Youzhou was re-established to oversee the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月，命太子中允李寮為宣撫党項使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, Crown Prince Household Attendant Li Liao was appointed Commissioner to Pacify and Console the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year Li Liao, attendant to the crown prince, was appointed commissioner to pacify the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 以部落繁富，時遠近商賈，賫繒貨入貿羊馬。

translations.literal: Because the tribes were prosperous, merchants from near and far at times brought silks and goods in to trade for sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: As the tribes prospered, merchants from far and near brought silks and goods to trade for sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 至太和、開成之際，其籓鎮統領無緒，恣其貪婪，不顧危亡，或強市其羊馬，不酬其直，以是部落苦之，遂相率為盜，靈、鹽之路小梗。

translations.literal: By the Taihe and Kaicheng periods their frontier commanders' leadership was disorderly; they indulged their greed without regard for peril, sometimes forcibly buying their sheep and horses without paying fair price; because of this the tribes suffered, and they therefore banded together as bandits, and the roads of Ling and Yan were slightly obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taihe and Kaicheng eras frontier commanders ruled without discipline, greedily forcing purchases of sheep and horses without fair payment; the tribes suffered and turned to banditry, briefly disrupting traffic on the Ling and Yan routes.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，上頻命使安撫之，兼命憲臣為使，分三印以統之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang the emperor repeatedly ordered envoys to pacify them and also appointed censorial officials as commissioners, dividing three seals to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang reign the emperor repeatedly sent pacification envoys and appointed censorial commissioners, dividing authority among three seals.

sentences.zh: 在邠、寧、延者，以侍御史、內供奉崔君會主之；

translations.literal: Those in Bin, Ning, and Yan were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Cui Junhui;
translations.idiomatic: The Bin, Ning, and Yan groups were assigned to Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Cui Junhui;

sentences.zh: 在鹽、夏、長、澤者，以侍御史、內供奉李鄠主之；

translations.literal: those in Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Li E;
translations.idiomatic: those in Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze to Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Li E;

sentences.zh: 在靈、武、麟、勝者，以侍御史、內供奉鄭賀主之，仍各賜緋魚以重其事。

translations.literal: those in Ling, Wu, Lin, and Sheng were overseen by Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Zheng He; each was moreover granted crimson fish pouches to dignify the office.
translations.idiomatic: and those in Ling, Wu, Lin, and Sheng to Attending Censor and Inner Attendant Zheng He—each granted a crimson fish pouch to mark the importance of the mission.

sentences.zh: 久而無狀，尋皆罷之。

translations.literal: After a long while there was no result, and soon all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After long service with little to show for it, all were soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高昌高昌者，漢車師前王之庭，後漢戊己校尉之故地。

translations.literal: Gaochang—Gaochang was the court of the Former King of the Cheshi of Han and the old territory of the Wuji Colonel of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang was the seat of the Former Cheshi King under the Han and the former domain of the Later Han Wuji commandant.

sentences.zh: 在京師西四千三百里。

translations.literal: It lay four thousand three hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four thousand three hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 其國有二十一城，王都高昌。

translations.literal: The state had twenty-one cities, and the royal capital was Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom comprised twenty-one cities, with Gaochang as its capital.

sentences.zh: 其交河城，前王庭也；

translations.literal: Its Jiaohe city was the former royal court;
translations.idiomatic: Jiaohe was the former royal seat;

sentences.zh: 田地城，校尉城也。

translations.literal: Tiandicheng was the colonel's city.
translations.idiomatic: and Tiandicheng the commandant's garrison.

sentences.zh: 勝兵且萬人。

translations.literal: Fit soldiers numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Its fighting strength was nearly ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 厥土良沃，谷麥歲再熟；

translations.literal: Its soil was fertile and good; grain and wheat ripened twice a year;
translations.idiomatic: The soil was rich and grain ripened twice yearly;

sentences.zh: 有蒲萄酒，宜五果；

translations.literal: there was grape wine, and the five fruits flourished;
translations.idiomatic: grape wine was produced and all manner of fruit thrived;

sentences.zh: 有草名白疊，國人采其花，織以為布。

translations.literal: there was a plant called baidie; the people gathered its flowers and wove them into cloth.
translations.idiomatic: and a plant called baidie whose flowers the people wove into cloth.

sentences.zh: 有文字，知書計，所置官亦采中國之號焉。

translations.literal: They had writing and understood accounts; the offices they established also adopted designations from China.
translations.idiomatic: They had a written language and kept accounts, and their official titles followed Chinese usage.

sentences.zh: 其王麹伯雅，即後魏時高昌王嘉之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Their king Qu Boya was the sixth-generation descendant of King Jia of Gaochang in the Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Qu Boya was the sixth-generation descendant of Gaochang King Jia of the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時入朝，拜左光祿大夫、車師太守、封弁國公，仍以戚屬宇文氏女為華容公主以妻之，

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang of Sui he came to court and was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commandant of Cheshi, and enfeoffed as Duke of Bianguo; a daughter of the imperial Yuwen clan was made Princess Huarong and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui he visited the court and was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commandant of Cheshi, enfeoffed as Duke of Bianguo, and given Princess Huarong, a daughter of the Yuwen imperial clan, as his wife.

sentences.zh: 伯雅死，子文泰嗣，遣使來告哀，高祖遣前河州刺史硃惠表往吊之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, when Boya died his son Wentai succeeded him; envoys came to announce the mourning, and Gaozu sent former Hezhou Prefect Zhu Huibiao to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude (619), when Boya died his son Wentai succeeded him; envoys announced the death, and Gaozu sent former Hezhou prefect Zhu Huibiao to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 七年，文泰又獻狗雄雌各一，高六寸，長尺餘，性甚慧，能曳馬銜燭，雲本出拂菻國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Wentai again presented one male and one female dog, six inches in height and a little over a foot in length, very clever by nature, able to draw a horse's bridle and carry a candle; it was said they originally came from the land of Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Wentai presented a male and female dog, six inches tall and just over a foot long, remarkably clever and able to lead a horse by the bridle while carrying a candle—said to be native to Fulin (Byzantium).

sentences.zh: 中國有拂菻狗，自此始也。

translations.literal: China had Fulin dogs from this time onward.
translations.idiomatic: From this time China first had Fulin dogs.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，復貢玄狐裘，因賜其妻宇文氏花鈿一具。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Wentai again presented a black-fox fur robe, and Taizong thereupon bestowed on his wife Lady Yuwen a set of floral forehead ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Wentai again sent a black-fox fur robe, and the emperor in turn gave Lady Yuwen a set of floral forehead ornaments.

sentences.zh: 宇文氏復貢玉盤。

translations.literal: Lady Yuwen in turn presented a jade platter.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuwen reciprocated with a gift of a jade platter.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國所有動靜，輒以奏聞。

translations.literal: Whatever movements occurred among the Western Region states, he would report them at once.
translations.idiomatic: He reported every development among the Western Region kingdoms to the court.

sentences.zh: 冬，文泰來朝，及將歸蕃，賜遺甚厚。

translations.literal: In winter Wentai came to court, and when he was about to return to his realm, gifts and send-offs were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wentai came to court, and when he prepared to return home he was sent off with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 其妻宇文氏請預宗親，詔賜李氏，封常樂公主，下詔慰諭之。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Yuwen requested to be enrolled among the imperial kin; an edict granted her the surname Li, enfeoffed her as Princess Changle, and issued an edict to comfort and instruct her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yuwen asked to be enrolled among the imperial clan; she was granted the surname Li, created Princess Changle, and an edict of reassurance was issued.

sentences.zh: 時西戎諸國來朝貢者，皆塗經高昌，文泰後稍壅絕之。

translations.literal: At that time all Western Region states coming to court with tribute passed through Gaochang, but Wentai later gradually blocked and cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Western Region envoys bound for court all passed through Gaochang, but Wentai gradually began intercepting them.

sentences.zh: 伊吾先臣西突厥，至是內屬，文泰又與葉護連結，將擊伊吾。

translations.literal: Yiwu had first submitted to the Western Turks; by this time it submitted inwardly to China, but Wentai again allied with the Yabghu and was about to attack Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu had once served the Western Turks but now submitted to China; Wentai allied with the Yabghu and prepared to attack it.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其反覆，下書切讓，徵其大臣冠軍阿史那矩入朝，將與議事。

translations.literal: Taizong, because of his fickleness, sent a stern letter of rebuke and summoned his minister Champion Ashina Ju to court to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked him sharply in writing for his duplicity and summoned his minister Champion Ashina Ju to court for consultations.

sentences.zh: 文泰竟不遣，乃遣其長史麹雍來謝罪。

translations.literal: Wentai ultimately did not send him but instead dispatched his chief clerk Qu Yong to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai refused to send Ju and instead dispatched chief clerk Qu Yong to apologize.

sentences.zh: 初，大業之亂，中國人多投於突厥。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the disorders of the Daye era, many Chinese fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaos of the Daye era, many Chinese had fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 及頡利敗，或有奔高昌者，文泰皆拘留不遣。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, some fled to Gaochang; Wentai detained them all and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat, some fled to Gaochang, and Wentai detained them all.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔令括送，文泰尚隱蔽之。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered them rounded up and sent back, but Wentai still concealed them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered them rounded up and returned, but Wentai still hid them.

sentences.zh: 又尋與西突厥乙毗設擊破焉耆三城，虜其男女而去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again joined with the Western Turk Yipiqie to break Yanqi's three cities and carried off its men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the Western Turk Yipiqie in attacking three Yanqi cities and carried off their people.

sentences.zh: 焉耆王上表訴之，太宗遣虞部郎中李道裕往問其狀。

translations.literal: The King of Yanqi submitted a memorial of complaint; Taizong sent Director of the Palace Workshops Li Daoyu to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yanqi petitioned in protest, and Taizong sent Director Li Daoyu of the Palace Workshops to investigate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太宗謂其使曰：「高昌數年來朝貢脫略，無籓臣禮，國中署置官號，準我百僚，稱臣於人，豈得如此！

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Taizong said to their envoy: "For years Gaochang has come to court and presented tribute in a negligent, perfunctory manner, without the courtesy due a vassal. Within the state you establish offices and titles modeled on our hundred officials, yet you call yourselves subjects of others—how can this be?
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Taizong told their envoy: "For years Gaochang has sent tribute in a negligent manner, without proper vassal courtesy. You have established offices modeled on our bureaucracy, yet you also call yourselves subjects of others—how can this be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 今茲歲首，萬國來朝，而文泰不至。

translations.literal: Now at this year's beginning all states came to court, yet Wentai did not come.
translations.idiomatic: At this New Year all nations came to court, yet Wentai did not appear.

sentences.zh: 增城深塹，預備討伐。

translations.literal: You have added walls and deep moats, preparing for punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: You have strengthened your walls and moats in preparation for war.

sentences.zh: 日者我使人至彼，文泰云：『鷹飛於天，雉竄於蒿，貓遊於堂，鼠安於穴，各得其所，豈不活耶！』

translations.literal: The other day when my envoy reached you, Wentai said: 'The hawk flies in heaven, the pheasant hides in the weeds, the cat roams the hall, the rat rests in its hole—each has its place; are they not alive?
translations.idiomatic: When my envoy recently reached you, Wentai said: 'The hawk soars in the sky, the pheasant hides in the weeds, the cat roams the hall, the rat nests in its hole—each in its place; are they not content?

sentences.zh: 又西域使欲來者，文泰悉拘留之。

translations.literal: Moreover, envoys from the Western Regions wishing to come, Wentai detained them all.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he detained every Western Region envoy who wished to come to our court.

sentences.zh: 又遣使謂薛延陀云：『既自為可汗，與漢天子敵也，何須拜謁其使。』

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy to tell the Xueyantuo: 'Since you have made yourself qaghan, you are the equal of the Son of Heaven of Han—why need you bow to his envoys?
translations.idiomatic: He also told the Xueyantuo: 'Since you have made yourself qaghan, you are the equal of the Han emperor—why bow to his envoys?

sentences.zh: 事人闕禮，離間鄰好，惡而不誅，善者何勸？

translations.literal: In serving others he lacks courtesy, sows discord among neighbors—if the wicked are not punished, how are the good to be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: He lacks courtesy toward his superiors and sows discord among neighbors. If the wicked go unpunished, what incentive is there for the good?

sentences.zh: 明年，當發兵馬以擊爾。」

translations.literal: Next year I shall send troops and horses to attack you."
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall send an army against you."

sentences.zh: 是時薛延陀可汗表請為軍向導，以擊高昌，太宗許之。

translations.literal: At this time the Xueyantuo qaghan memorialized requesting to serve as army guide to attack Gaochang, and Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Xueyantuo qaghan offered to guide the army against Gaochang, and Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 令民部尚書唐儉至延陀，與謀進取。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to go to the Xueyantuo to plan the advance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to the Xueyantuo to coordinate the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太宗冀其悔過，復下璽書，示以禍福，徵之入朝。

translations.literal: Taizong hoped he would repent, and again issued an imperial sealed letter showing fortune and disaster, summoning him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping Wentai would repent, Taizong again sent a sealed edict explaining the consequences and summoning him to court.

sentences.zh: 文泰稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Wentai claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃命吏部尚書侯君集為交河道大總管，率左屯衛大將軍薛萬均及突厥、契、苾之眾，步騎數萬眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon appointed Minister of Personnel Hou Junji Grand Commander of the Jiaohe Circuit, leading Left Garrison Guard General Xue Wanjun and the masses of Turks, Qibi, and Tiele—several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry—to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then appointed Minister of Personnel Hou Junji grand commander of the Jiaohe campaign, with Left Garrison Guard General Xue Wanjun and tens of thousands of Turkish, Qibi, and Tiele infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時公卿近臣，皆以行經沙磧，萬里用兵，恐難得志；

translations.literal: At that time high ministers and close officials all said that marching through desert sands and waging war ten thousand li away, they feared success would be hard to achieve;
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that marching across the desert to fight a war ten thousand li away was unlikely to succeed;

sentences.zh: 又界居絕域，縱得之，不可以守，競以為諫。

translations.literal: moreover the border lay in a remote region—even if gained, it could not be held—and they all competed in offering remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: and that even if conquered, the remote territory could not be held—they all urged against the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太宗皆不聽。

translations.literal: Taizong would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 文泰謂所親曰：「吾往者朝覲，見秦、隴之北，城邑蕭條，非復有隋之比。

translations.literal: Wentai said to his intimates: "When I went before to court audience, I saw north of Qin and Long that cities and towns were desolate—not like the Sui anymore.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai told his intimates: "When I last visited court, I saw that north of Qin and Long the cities were desolate—nothing like the Sui era.

sentences.zh: 設今伐我，發兵多則糧運不給；

translations.literal: Suppose they now attack me—if they send many troops, grain transport will not suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If they attack now, a large army cannot be supplied;

sentences.zh: 若發三萬以下，吾能制之。

translations.literal: if they send fewer than thirty thousand, I can control them.
translations.idiomatic: if they send fewer than thirty thousand, I can handle them.

sentences.zh: 加以磧路艱險，自然疲頓，吾以逸待勞，坐收其弊，何足為憂也？」

translations.literal: Moreover the desert route is hard and dangerous—they will naturally grow weary; I shall await them at ease while they labor, and sit to collect their exhaustion—what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: The desert route is arduous and will wear them down; I shall meet their fatigue with rested troops—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 及聞王師臨磧口，惶駭計無所出，發病而死。

translations.literal: When he heard the imperial army had reached the desert pass, he was terrified and could devise no plan; he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the imperial army had reached the desert pass, terror left him helpless; he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 其子智盛嗣立。

translations.literal: His son Zhicheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhicheng succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而君集兵奄至柳谷，進趨田地城，將軍契苾何力為前軍，與之接戰而退。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Junji's army suddenly arrived at Liugu, advanced toward Tiandicheng; General Qibi Heli as vanguard engaged them in battle and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Junji's army soon reached Liugu and advanced on Tiandicheng; General Qibi Heli led the vanguard, skirmished, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大軍繼之，攻拔其城，虜男女七千餘口。

translations.literal: The main army followed, stormed and took the city, and captured more than seven thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The main force followed, stormed the city, and took more than seven thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 進逼其都。

translations.literal: They advanced to press the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They then pressed on the capital.

sentences.zh: 智盛移君集書曰：「有罪於天子者，先王也，咎深譴積，身已喪亡。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent Junji a letter saying: "He who offended the Son of Heaven was my late father; his guilt was deep and punishment long accumulated, and he has already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng wrote to Junji: "The offense against the Son of Heaven was my father's; his guilt was deep and he is already dead.

sentences.zh: 智盛襲位無幾，君其赦諸？」

translations.literal: Zhicheng has succeeded only a short while—will you not pardon me?"
translations.idiomatic: I have only just succeeded—will you not show mercy?"

sentences.zh: 君集謂曰：「若能悔禍，當面縛軍門也。」

translations.literal: Junji said to him: "If you can repent your disaster, you must come bound before the camp gate."
translations.idiomatic: Junji replied: "If you repent, come bound before the camp gate."

sentences.zh: 又命諸軍引沖車、拋車以逼之，飛石雨下，城中大懼。

translations.literal: He also ordered the armies to bring battering rams and catapults to press the city; flying stones rained down and the city was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered battering rams and catapults forward; stones rained down and panic gripped the city.

sentences.zh: 智盛窮蹙，出城降。

translations.literal: Zhicheng, cornered, came out of the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng, trapped, came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 君集分兵掠地，下其三郡、五縣、二十二城。

translations.literal: Junji divided troops to overrun the land, taking its three commanderies, five counties, and twenty-two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Junji sent detachments to overrun the territory, taking three commanderies, five counties, and twenty-two cities.

sentences.zh: 戶八千，口三萬七千七百，馬四千三百匹。

translations.literal: Households eight thousand, persons thirty-seven thousand seven hundred, horses four thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The tally was eight thousand households, thirty-seven thousand seven hundred people, and four thousand three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 其界東西八百里，南北五百里。

translations.literal: Its borders were eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory measured eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 先是，其國童謠云：「高昌兵馬如霜雪，漢家兵馬如日月。

translations.literal: Earlier, a children's song in the state said: "Gaochang's troops and horses are like frost and snow; Han's troops and horses are like sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's song had run: "Gaochang's armies are frost and snow; the Han armies are sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 日月照霜雪，回手自消滅。」

translations.literal: Sun and moon shine on frost and snow, and turning the hand they vanish of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon shine on frost and snow, it melts away at a turn of the hand."

sentences.zh: 文泰使人捕其初唱者，不能得。

translations.literal: Wentai sent men to seize whoever first sang it but could not find them.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai sent men to seize whoever first sang it but could not find them.

sentences.zh: 初，文泰與西突厥欲谷設通和，遺其金帛，約有急相為表裏。

translations.literal: Earlier Wentai had been on friendly terms with the Western Turk Yugu She, sent him gold and silks, and agreed that in emergency they would aid each other inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai had allied with the Western Turk Yugu She, sending him gold and silks with a pact of mutual aid in crisis.

sentences.zh: 及聞君集兵至，欲谷設懼而西走，不敢救。

translations.literal: When he heard Junji's army had arrived, Yugu She was afraid and fled west, not daring to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Junji was coming, Yugu She fled west in fear and dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 君集尋遣使告捷，太宗大悅，宴白僚，班賜各有差。

translations.literal: Junji soon sent envoys to report victory; Taizong was greatly pleased, feasted all officials, and distributed rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Junji soon reported victory; Taizong was delighted, feasted the officials, and distributed rewards by rank.

sentences.zh: 曲赦高昌部內從軍兵士已上，父子犯死罪已下，期親犯流已下，大功犯徒已下，小功緦麻犯杖罪，悉原之。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted within Gaochang for soldiers and above who served in the army: fathers and sons guilty of capital crimes and below, close kin guilty of exile and below, great-achievement kin guilty of penal servitude and below, lesser and distant kin guilty of beating— all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for Gaochang soldiers and above, pardoning capital crimes between fathers and sons, exile among close kin, penal servitude among those of great-achievement mourning, and beating among lesser and distant kin.

sentences.zh: 時太宗欲以高昌為州縣，特進魏徵諫曰：「陛下初臨天下，高昌夫婦先來朝謁。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong wished to make Gaochang into prefectures and counties; Special Advancement Holder Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Your Majesty first came to rule the realm, the Gaochang couple came first to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wished to convert Gaochang into prefectures and counties; Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, the Gaochang king and queen were among the first to pay court.

sentences.zh: 自後數月，商胡被其遏絕貢獻，加之不禮大國，遂使五誅載加。

translations.literal: Within a few months afterward, merchant foreigners were blocked by him from tribute, and moreover he was discourteous to the great state—thus the five punishments were heaped upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Within months, merchant envoys were blocked from tribute, and discourtesy toward the empire brought the five punishments upon him.

sentences.zh: 若罪止文泰，斯亦可矣，未若撫其人而立其子，所謂伐罪吊民，威德被於遐外，為國之善者也。

translations.literal: If guilt stopped with Wentai, that would also do; better yet to comfort the people and establish his son—what is called punishing crime and consoling the people, with authority and virtue reaching distant regions—is the good policy for a state.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing Wentai alone would suffice; better still to comfort the people and install his son—punishing the guilty while succoring the people, spreading authority to distant lands—is the wise policy.

sentences.zh: 今若利其土壤，以為州縣，常須千餘人鎮守，數年一易，每及交蕃，死者十有三四，遣辦衣資，離別親戚，十年之後，隴右空虛。

translations.literal: Now if you take their soil for profit and make it prefectures and counties, you will constantly need more than a thousand men to garrison it, replaced every few years; each time they cross the frontier, three or four in ten die; sending them to prepare clothing and supplies, parting from kin—after ten years Longyou will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: If you seize their land for prefectures and counties, you will need a thousand garrison troops rotated every few years; three or four in ten die crossing the frontier, leaving families behind—within ten years Longyou will be drained.

sentences.zh: 陛下終不得高昌撮谷尺布以助中國，所謂散有用而事無用，臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty will ultimately not obtain from Gaochang even a pinch of grain or a foot of cloth to aid China—what is called scattering the useful while serving the useless; your servant does not see how this can be approved."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will never receive even a pinch of grain from Gaochang to aid the empire—scattering useful resources on a useless enterprise. I see no merit in this."

sentences.zh: 太宗不從，竟以其地置西州，又置安西都護府，留兵以鎮之。

translations.literal: Taizong did not follow this advice and ultimately established Xizhou on their land, also set up the Protectorate General of Anxi, and left troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rejected the advice, established Xizhou on the conquered land, set up the Anxi Protectorate, and left a garrison.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥遣其葉護，屯兵於可汗浮圖城，與高昌相影響，至是懼而來降，以其地為庭州。

translations.literal: Earlier the Western Turks had sent their Yabghu to station troops at Qaghan Stupa City, mutually supporting Gaochang; at this they were afraid and came to surrender, and their land was made Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks had stationed their Yabghu at Qaghan Stupa City in support of Gaochang; now they surrendered in fear, and their territory became Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是勒石紀功而旋。

translations.literal: Thereupon they carved stone to record the achievement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A stone monument was erected to record the victory, and the army returned.

sentences.zh: 其智盛君臣及其豪右，皆徙中國。

translations.literal: Zhicheng's courtiers and ministers and their powerful families were all relocated to China.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng, his court, and the leading families were all relocated to China.

sentences.zh: 麹氏有國，至智盛凡九世，一百三十四年而滅。

translations.literal: The Qu clan held the state; down to Zhicheng there were nine generations in all, one hundred thirty-four years, then extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu dynasty ruled for nine generations and one hundred thirty-four years until Zhicheng's fall.

sentences.zh: 尋拜智盛為左武衛將軍，封金城郡公；

translations.literal: Soon Zhicheng was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Jincheng Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng was soon appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and created Duke of Jincheng;

sentences.zh: 弟智湛為右武衛中郎將，天山縣公。

translations.literal: his younger brother Zhizhan was made Middle General of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Tianshan County.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Zhizhan was made Middle General of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Tianshan County.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，刊石像智盛之形，列於昭陵玄闕之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, a stone image of Zhicheng's form was carved and set below the Dark Gate of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, a stone statue of Zhicheng was carved and placed below the Dark Gate of Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 智湛，麟德中終於左驍衛大將軍、西州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhizhan, in the Linde era, ended his career as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhan died in the Linde era as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 天授初，其子崇裕授左武衛大將軍，交阿郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou his son Chongyu was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and Prince of Jiao'a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou era his son Chongyu was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and Prince of Jiao'a.

sentences.zh: 卒，封襲遂絕。

translations.literal: When he died, the enfeoffment and succession came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the line of enfeoffment ended.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾吐谷渾，其先居於徒河之清山，屬晉亂，始度隴，止於甘松之南，洮水之西，南極白蘭，地數千里。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun—Tuyuhun's ancestors dwelt at Clear Mountain on the Tuo River; when the Jin fell into disorder they first crossed Long, stopping south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, reaching south to Bailan—lands of several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun—Tuyuhun's ancestors lived at Clear Mountain on the Tuo River; during the Jin disorders they crossed Long into the region south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, extending south to Bailan over several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 有城郭而不居，隨逐水草，廬帳為室，肉酪為糧。

translations.literal: They had walled towns but did not dwell in them, following water and pasture; felt tents were their chambers, meat and curds their food.
translations.idiomatic: They had walled towns but did not live in them, following pasture and water; felt tents were their homes, meat and dairy their food.

sentences.zh: 其官初有長史、司馬、將軍。

translations.literal: Their offices at first had Chief Clerk, Marshal, and General.
translations.idiomatic: Their government at first had chief clerks, marshals, and generals.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，有王公、僕射、尚書、郎中。

translations.literal: In recent times there have been princes, dukes, Grand Masters, Ministers, and Directors.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times they have had princes, dukes, grandees, ministers, and directors.

sentences.zh: 其俗頗識文字。

translations.literal: Their customs show considerable knowledge of writing.
translations.idiomatic: They have some knowledge of writing.

sentences.zh: 男子通服長裙繒帽，或戴冪苾，婦人以金花為首飾，辮髮縈後，綴以珠貝。

translations.literal: Men generally wore long skirts, silk caps, or wore felt hoods; women used golden flowers as head ornaments, braided hair wound behind, adorned with pearls and shells.
translations.idiomatic: Men generally wore long robes and silk caps or felt hoods; women wore golden floral head ornaments, braided hair wound behind, and strings of pearls and shells.

sentences.zh: 其婚姻富家厚出聘財，貧人竊女而去。

translations.literal: In marriage wealthy families gave lavish betrothal gifts; poor men stole girls and took them away.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families gave lavish betrothal gifts; poor men abducted brides.

sentences.zh: 父卒，妻其庶母；

translations.literal: When the father died, they married his concubines;
translations.idiomatic: When a father died, sons married his concubines;

sentences.zh: 兄亡，妻其諸嫂。

translations.literal: when the elder brother died, they married his sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: when an elder brother died, younger brothers married his widows.

sentences.zh: 喪有服制，葬訖而除。

translations.literal: Mourning had garment regulations; when burial was finished mourning was removed.
translations.idiomatic: They observed mourning garments, which were laid aside after burial.

sentences.zh: 國無常稅，用度不給，輒斂富室商人，以取足而止。

translations.literal: The state had no regular taxes; when expenses were insufficient they would levy wealthy households and merchants until enough was obtained and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: There were no regular taxes; when funds ran short they levied wealthy households and merchants until enough was raised.

sentences.zh: 殺人及盜馬者罪死，他犯則徵物以贖罪。

translations.literal: Murderers and horse thieves were punished with death; for other offenses goods were levied to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Murder and horse theft were capital crimes; other offenses were redeemed with goods.

sentences.zh: 氣候多寒，土宜大麥、蔓菁，頗有菽粟。

translations.literal: The climate was mostly cold; the soil suited barley and turnips, and there was considerable beans and millet.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was cold; barley and turnips grew well, and beans and millet were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 出良馬、牦牛、銅、鐵、硃砂之類。

translations.literal: They produced fine horses, yaks, copper, iron, cinnabar, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: They produced fine horses, yaks, copper, iron, cinnabar, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 有青海，周回八百里，中有小山，至冬，放牝馬於其上，言得龍種。

translations.literal: There was Qinghai Lake, eight hundred li in circumference; within it was a small hill; in winter they released brood mares upon it, saying they obtained dragon stock.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake measured eight hundred li around; on a small island within it, brood mares were turned loose each winter, said to breed with dragons.

sentences.zh: 嘗得波斯馬，放入海，因生驄駒，能日行千里，故代稱「青海驄」焉。

translations.literal: They once obtained Persian horses and released them into the lake; thereby zong colts were born, able to travel a thousand li in a day—hence they were called in successive ages "Qinghai Zong."
translations.idiomatic: Persian stallions were once turned loose in the lake, producing zong foals said to run a thousand li a day—hence the famed Qinghai zong horses.

sentences.zh: 地兼鄯善、且沫。

translations.literal: Their territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 西北有流沙數百里，夏有熱風，傷弊行旅，風之將至，老駝便知之，則引項而鳴，以口鼻埋沙中。

translations.literal: To the northwest were drifting sands several hundred li; in summer there were hot winds that harmed travelers; when the wind was about to come, old camels knew it, stretched their necks and cried, and buried their muzzles in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lay drifting sands hundreds of li across; in summer hot winds killed travelers. Old camels sensed the wind's approach, stretched their necks and cried, and buried their muzzles in the sand.

sentences.zh: 人以為候，即以氈擁蔽口鼻而避其患。

translations.literal: People took this as a sign and used felt to cover and shield mouth and nose to avoid the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers took this as a warning and wrapped felt over their faces to survive.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，其王伏允來犯塞，煬帝親總六軍以討之，伏允以數十騎潛於泥嶺而遁，其仙頭王率男女十餘萬口來降。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang of Sui, their king Fuyun came to raid the frontier; Emperor Yang personally commanded the Six Armies to campaign against him; Fuyun with several dozen horsemen slipped away hidden at Niling, while his Xiandou king led more than a hundred thousand men and women to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, King Fuyun raided the frontier; the emperor personally led the Six Armies against him. Fuyun escaped with a few dozen horsemen at Niling, while his Xiandou king surrendered with more than a hundred thousand people.

sentences.zh: 煬帝立其質子順為王，送之本國，令統餘眾，尋復追還。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang installed his hostage Shun as king, sent him back to his native state to command the remaining masses, but soon recalled him again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang installed his hostage Shun as king and sent him home to rule the remnant people, but soon recalled him.

sentences.zh: 大業末，伏允悉收故地，復為邊患。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Fuyun recovered all the old lands and again became a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daye era Fuyun had recovered all his former territory and again threatened the frontier.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，順自江都來歸長安。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Shun came from Jiangdu to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shun returned from Jiangdu to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時李軌猶據涼州，高祖遣使與伏允通和，令擊軌以自效，當放順返國。

translations.literal: At that time Li Gui still held Liangzhou; Gaozu sent envoys to make peace with Fuyun, ordering him to attack Gui to prove his merit, whereupon Shun would be released to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui still held Liangzhou; Gaozu sent envoys to Fuyun offering peace if he attacked Li Gui, promising to return Shun.

sentences.zh: 伏允大悅，興兵擊之，戰於庫門，交綏而退。

translations.literal: Fuyun was greatly pleased, raised troops to attack him, fought at Kumen, clashed briefly and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun gladly raised troops, fought Li Gui at Kumen, skirmished, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 頻遣使朝貢，以順為請，高祖乃遣之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys with tribute, requesting Shun; Gaozu thereupon sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute repeatedly, asking for Shun's return, and Gaozu sent him home.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，伏允遣其洛陽公來朝。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Fuyun sent his Duke of Luoyang to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Fuyun sent his Duke of Luoyang to court.

sentences.zh: 使未返，大掠鄯州而去。

translations.literal: Before the envoy returned, he launched a great raid on Qinzhou and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy returned, Fuyun launched a major raid on Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使責讓之，徵伏允入朝，稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Taizong sent envoys to rebuke and reproach him and summoned Fuyun to court; he claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent envoys to rebuke him and summon Fuyun to court; he pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 仍為其子尊王求婚，於是責其親迎以羈縻之。

translations.literal: Still on behalf of his son Lord Zun he sought marriage; thereupon [the court] required him to come in person to welcome the bride in order to keep him on a tether.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun still sought a marriage alliance through his son Lord Zun; the court then required him to come in person to fetch the bride, intending to bind him by marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 尊王又稱疾不肯入朝，有詔停婚，遣中郎將康處直諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Lord Zun again claimed illness and refused to come to court; there was an edict stopping the marriage, and Palace Gentleman Kang Chuzhi was sent to instruct him on fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zun again pleaded illness and refused to attend court; the emperor canceled the marriage and sent Palace Gentleman Kang Chuzhi to warn him of the consequences.

sentences.zh: 伏允遣兵寇蘭、廓二州。

translations.literal: Fuyun sent troops to raid the two prefectures of Lan and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun sent troops to raid Lan and Kuo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時鄯州刺史李玄運上言：「吐谷渾良馬悉牧青海，輕兵掩之，可致大利。」

translations.literal: At the time Qinzhou Prefect Li Xuanyun submitted a memorial: "Tuyuhun's fine horses are all pastured at Qinghai; with light troops to make a surprise attack, great profit can be gained."
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou Prefect Li Xuanyun memorialized: "Tuyuhun's finest horses graze around Qinghai. A light raid would yield great spoils.

sentences.zh: 於是遣左驍衛大將軍段志玄率邊兵及契苾、党項之眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Xiaoqiwei Grand General Duan Zhixuan was sent leading frontier troops and the masses of Qibi and Tangut to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Left Xiaoqiwei Grand General Duan Zhixuan with frontier troops and Qibi and Tangut allies to attack them.

sentences.zh: 去青海三十里，志玄與左驍衛將軍梁洛仁不欲戰，頓軍遲留不進，吐谷渾遂驅青海牧馬而遁。

translations.literal: Thirty li from Qinghai, Zhixuan and Left Xiaoqiwei General Liang Luoren did not wish to fight, halted the army and lingered without advancing; Tuyuhun then drove off the Qinghai pasture horses and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Qinghai, Duan Zhixuan and Left Xiaoqiwei General Liang Luoren held back and would not fight; Tuyuhun drove off the Qinghai herds and escaped.

sentences.zh: 亞將李君羨率精騎別路，及賊於青海之南懸水鎮，擊破之，虜牛羊二萬餘頭而還。

translations.literal: Deputy general Li Junxian led elite cavalry by a separate route, caught the bandits at Xuanshui garrison south of Qinghai, defeated them, and captured more than twenty thousand head of cattle and sheep before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Li Junxian took elite cavalry by another route, caught the enemy at Xuanshui south of Qinghai, routed them, and returned with more than twenty thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 時伏允年老昏耄，其邪臣天柱王惑亂之，拘我行人鴻臚丞趙德楷。

translations.literal: At the time Fuyun was old and senile; his wicked minister the Tianzhu King confused and disturbed him, and detained our traveling envoy Honglu Vice Director Zhao Dekai.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fuyun was old and feeble; his corrupt minister the Tianzhu King misled him and seized our envoy, Honglu Vice Director Zhao Dekai.

sentences.zh: 太宗頻遣宣諭，使者十餘返，竟無悛心，

translations.literal: Taizong repeatedly sent proclamations and instructions; envoys returned more than ten times, yet in the end there was no mind to repent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent repeated admonitions; more than ten envoys went back and forth, but Fuyun showed no sign of repentance.

sentences.zh: 詔特進李靖為西海道行軍大總管；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict appointed Special Advance Li Jing as Grand Commander of the Xihai Route Army;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict appointed Li Jing, Special Advance, grand commander of the Xihai Route army;

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書侯君集為積石道行軍總管，任城王道宗為鄯州道行軍總管，仍為靖副；

translations.literal: Minister of War Hou Junji as Commander of the Jishi Route Army, Prince Daizong of Rencheng as Commander of the Qinzhou Route Army, still serving as Jing's deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Hou Junji as commander of the Jishi Route army, Prince Daizong of Rencheng as commander of the Qinzhou Route army and Li Jing's deputy;

sentences.zh: 涼州都督李大亮為且沫道行軍總管，岷州都督李道彥為赤水道行軍總管，利州刺史高甑生為鹽澤道行軍總管，並突厥、契苾之眾以擊之。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Protector-General Li Daliang as Commander of the Qiemom Route Army, Minzhou Protector-General Li Daoyan as Commander of the Chishui Route Army, Lizhou Prefect Gao Zengsheng as Commander of the Yanzhe Route Army, all together with Turkic and Qibi masses to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou Protector-General Li Daliang as commander of the Qiemom Route army, Minzhou Protector-General Li Daoyan of the Chishui Route, Lizhou Prefect Gao Zengsheng of the Yanzhe Route, together with Turkic and Qibi forces to attack Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 諸將頻與賊遇，連戰破之，獲其高昌王慕容孝雋。

translations.literal: The generals frequently encountered the bandits, defeated them in successive battles, and captured their Gaochang king Murong Xiaojun.
translations.idiomatic: The generals met the enemy again and again, winning successive victories and capturing their Gaochang king, Murong Xiaojun.

sentences.zh: 孝雋有雄略，伏允心膂之臣也。

translations.literal: Xiaojun had bold strategy; he was Fuyun's trusted inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojun was a man of bold strategy and one of Fuyun's closest advisers.

sentences.zh: 靖等進至赤海，遇其天柱三部落，擊大破之，遂歷於河源。

translations.literal: Jing and the others advanced to Chihai, encountered their Tianzhu three tribes, inflicted a great defeat, and then passed through to the headwaters region.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's forces advanced to Chihai, routed the Tianzhu confederation in a great victory, and pressed on to the Yellow River headwaters.

sentences.zh: 李大亮又俘其名王二十人，雜畜數萬，至且沫西境，或傳伏允西走，渡圖倫磧，欲入於闐。

translations.literal: Li Daliang also captured twenty of their famous kings and tens of thousands of mixed livestock; when they reached the western border of Qiemom, some reported that Fuyun had fled west, crossing the Tulun desert, intending to enter Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang also took twenty noble captives and tens of thousands of livestock; at the western edge of Qiemom, reports said Fuyun had fled west across the Tulun Desert toward Khotan.

sentences.zh: 將軍薛萬均率輕銳追奔，入磧數百里，及其餘黨，破之。

translations.literal: General Xue Wanjun led light elite troops in pursuit, entered the desert several hundred li, caught up with the remnant faction, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: General Xue Wanjun pursued with light cavalry, rode several hundred li into the desert, overtook the remnant force, and destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 磧中乏水，將士皆刺馬血而飲之。

translations.literal: Water was scarce in the desert; officers and soldiers all pierced horse blood and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Water ran out in the desert, and the men pierced their horses' veins and drank the blood.

sentences.zh: 侯君集與江夏王道宗趣南路，登漢哭山，飲馬烏海，獲其名王梁屈忽，經塗二千餘里空虛之地，盛夏降霜，多積雪，其地乏水草，將士啖冰，馬皆食雪。

translations.literal: Hou Junji and Prince Daizong of Jiangxia took the southern route, ascended Hanku Mountain, watered horses at Wu Sea, captured their famous king Liang Quhu; they passed through more than two thousand li of empty land; in midsummer frost fell and snow accumulated heavily; the land lacked water and fodder; officers and soldiers ate ice, and horses all ate snow.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji and Prince Daizong of Jiangxia took the southern route, climbed Hanku Mountain, watered their horses at Wu Sea, and captured the noble Liang Quhu. They crossed more than two thousand li of empty country where frost fell in midsummer and snow lay deep; with no water or grass, the men ate ice and the horses ate snow.

sentences.zh: 又達於柏梁，北望積石山，觀河源之所出焉。

translations.literal: They also reached Bailiang, looked north at Jishi Mountain, and observed the place where the Yellow River's headwaters emerge.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Bailiang, gazed north toward Jishi Mountain, and looked upon the source of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 兩軍會於大非川，至破邏貞谷，伏允子大寧王順窮蹙，斬其國相天柱王，舉國來降。

translations.literal: The two armies joined at Dafei River and reached Poluozhen Valley; Fuyun's son Daining King Shun was cornered, beheaded the state chancellor Tianzhu King, and the whole state came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies met at the Dafei River and pushed into Poluozhen Valley; Fuyun's son Daining King Shun, hard pressed, killed his chancellor the Tianzhu King and surrendered with the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 伏允大懼，與千餘騎遁於磧中，眾稍亡散，能屬之者才百餘騎，乃自縊而死。

translations.literal: Fuyun was greatly afraid; with more than a thousand horsemen he fled into the desert; the masses gradually scattered and fled; those who could follow him were only a bit more than a hundred horsemen; he then hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled in terror with a thousand riders into the desert; his followers dwindled until barely a hundred remained, and he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 國人乃立順為可汗，稱臣內附。

translations.literal: The people of the state then installed Shun as khan, declared themselves subjects, and submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun then enthroned Shun as khan and submitted to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 順，即伏允之嫡子也。

translations.literal: Shun was precisely Fuyun's eldest son by the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was Fuyun's eldest son by his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 初為侍子於隋，拜金紫光祿大夫，久不得歸，伏允遂立他子為太子，及得返國，意常怏怏。

translations.literal: Initially he was a hostage at the Sui court, was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, long unable to return; Fuyun then installed another son as crown prince; when he obtained return to his state, his mind was often discontented.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served as a hostage at the Sui court, where he held the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; unable to return for years, he watched Fuyun install another son as heir. When he finally came home, he remained resentful.

sentences.zh: 會李靖等諸軍所向克捷，自以失位，欲因此立功，由是遂降。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jing and the other armies wherever they went achieved victories; he himself felt he had lost his position and wished thereby to achieve merit; on this account he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing's armies swept to victory on every front, Shun saw his chance to recover standing by a timely surrender, and so he submitted.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Taizong thereupon issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 太宗恐順不能靜其國，仍遣李大亮率精兵數千，為其聲援。

translations.literal: Taizong feared Shun could not pacify his state; still sent Li Daliang leading several thousand elite troops as his vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shun could not stabilize the realm, Taizong sent Li Daliang with several thousand elite troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 順既久質於隋，國人不附，未幾為臣下所殺。

translations.literal: Shun had long been a hostage at Sui; the people of the state did not attach to him; before long he was killed by subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shun had spent so many years as a hostage at the Sui court that his people never rallied to him, and before long his own officials killed him.

sentences.zh: 其子燕王諾曷缽嗣立。

translations.literal: His son the Yan Prince Nuohebo succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Yan Prince Nuohebo, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽既幼，大臣爭權，國中大亂。

translations.literal: Nuohebo being still young, great ministers contended for power, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo was still a child; rival ministers fought for power and the realm fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣兵援之，封為河源郡王。

translations.literal: Taizong sent troops to aid him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent troops to support him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 仍授烏地也拔勒豆可汗，遣淮陽王道明持節冊拜，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: Still invested him as Wudiyebaledou Khan, sent Prince Daoming of Huaiyang bearing credentials to invest and appoint him, and bestowed drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: He was also invested as Wudiyebaledou Khan; Prince Daoming of Huaiyang was sent with credentials to confirm the title and was given drums and battle standards.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽因入朝請婚。

translations.literal: Nuohebo thereupon came to court to request marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo then came to court to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太宗以弘化公主妻之，資送甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Taizong gave him Princess Honghua as wife, with very generous dowry and send-off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Taizong gave him Princess Honghua in marriage with a lavish dowry.

sentences.zh: 十五年，諾曷缽所部丞相王專權，陰謀作難。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Chancellor Wang of Nuohebo's division monopolized power and secretly plotted to raise trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Chancellor Wang of Nuohebo's court seized power and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 將征兵，詐言祭山神，因欲襲擊公主，劫諾曷缽奔於吐蕃，期有日矣。

translations.literal: About to levy troops, he falsely claimed to sacrifice to the mountain god; thereby he intended to surprise and attack the princess, seize Nuohebo, and flee to Tibet; the day was already set.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to mobilize troops under the pretense of offering sacrifice to a mountain god, planning to seize the princess, abduct Nuohebo, and flee to Tibet; the day was already fixed.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽知而大懼，率輕騎走鄯善城，其威信王以兵迎之。

translations.literal: Nuohebo learned of it and was greatly afraid; he led light cavalry and fled to Shanshan city, and his Weixin King came with troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Nuohebo learned of the plot he fled in terror with a light escort to Shanshan, where the Weixin King met him with troops.

sentences.zh: 鄯州刺史杜鳳舉與威信王合軍擊丞相王，破之，殺其兄弟三人，遣使言狀。
