translations.literal: Qinzhou Prefect Du Fengju joined forces with the Weixin King to attack Chancellor Wang, defeated him, killed his three brothers, and sent envoys to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou Prefect Du Fengju combined forces with the Weixin King, defeated Chancellor Wang, killed him and his three brothers, and reported the affair to the court.

sentences.zh: 太宗命民部尚書唐儉持節撫慰之。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian, bearing credentials, to go and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Minister of Revenue Tang Jian with credentials to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，刻石圖諾曷缽之形，列於昭陵之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, a stone was carved with the likeness of Nuohebo and arrayed below Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, a stone carving of Nuohebo was placed among the figures below Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，以其尚主，拜駙馬都尉，賜物四十段。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, because he had married an imperial princess, he was appointed Chief Commandant of the Empress's Relatives and given forty bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Nuohebo was made Chief Commandant of the Empress's Relatives because he had married a Tang princess, and was granted forty bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 其後與吐蕃互相攻伐，各遣使請兵救援，高宗皆不許之。

translations.literal: Afterward they and Tibet mutually attacked one another; each side sent envoys requesting troops for rescue, and Gaozong refused all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tuyuhun and Tibet fought each other repeatedly; both sides asked Gaozong for military aid, and he refused each request.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大怒，率兵以擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Tibet was greatly angered and led troops to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tibet marched against Tuyuhun in force.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽既不能禦，脫身及弘化公主走投涼州。

translations.literal: Nuohebo being unable to resist, he escaped with Princess Honghua and fled in distress to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to resist, Nuohebo fled with Princess Honghua to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣右威衛大將軍薛仁貴等救吐谷渾，為吐蕃所敗，於是吐谷渾遂為吐蕃所並。

translations.literal: Gaozong sent Right Weiwuwei Grand General Xue Rengui and others to rescue Tuyuhun; they were defeated by Tibet; thereupon Tuyuhun was annexed by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong sent Right Weiwuwei Grand General Xue Rengui to relieve Tuyuhun, but Tibet defeated him, and Tuyuhun was absorbed by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽以親信數千帳來內屬，詔左武衛大將軍蘇定方為安置大使，始徙其部眾於靈州之地，置安樂州，以諾曷缽為刺史，欲其安而且樂也，

translations.literal: Nuohebo came to submit internally with several thousand households of close followers; an edict appointed Left Wuweiwei Grand General Su Dingfang as Settlement Commissioner; for the first time his tribal masses were moved to the territory of Lingzhou; Anle Prefecture was established, with Nuohebo as prefect, intending that they be secure and moreover happy.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo submitted with several thousand loyal households; Su Dingfang, Left Wuweiwei Grand General, was appointed commissioner to resettle them. His people were moved for the first time to Lingzhou, where Anle Prefecture was created with Nuohebo as prefect—a name chosen so they might live in peace and contentment.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽卒，子忠嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong, Nuohebo died; his son Zhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chuigong, Nuohebo died and was succeeded by his son Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠卒，子宣趙嗣，

translations.literal: Zhong died; his son Xuanzhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong died, his son Xuanzhao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 授宣趙左豹韜衛員外大將軍，仍襲父烏地也拔勒豆可汗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenglong, Xuanzhao was appointed Outside Grand General of the Left Baotao Guard and still inherited his father's title of Wudiyebaledou Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenglong, Xuanzhao was made Outside Grand General of the Left Baotao Guard and inherited his father's title of Wudiyebaledou Khan.

sentences.zh: 宣趙卒，子曦皓嗣。

translations.literal: Xuanzhao died; his son Xihao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzhao died, his son Xihao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 曦皓卒，子兆嗣，及吐蕃陷我安樂州，其部眾又東徙，散在朔方、河東之境。

translations.literal: Xihao died; his son Zhao succeeded; when Tibet captured our Anle Prefecture, his tribal masses again moved east and scattered through the territories of Shuofang and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xihao died, his son Zhao succeeded him; after Tibet overran Anle Prefecture, the Tuyuhun moved east again and scattered across Shuofang and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 今俗多謂之退渾，蓋語急而然。

translations.literal: Today in common speech they are often called Tuihun; this is probably because speech is hurried and so becomes thus.
translations.idiomatic: Today people often call them Tuihun—a shortened form of the name in quick speech.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以朔方節度副使、左金吾衛大將軍同正慕容復為襲長樂州都督、青海國王、烏地也拔勒豆可汗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Shuofang Circuit deputy military commissioner and Left Jinwuwei Grand General of equal rank Murong Fu was appointed to inherit the posts of Protector-General of Changle Prefecture, King of Qinghai, and Wudiyebaledou Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Murong Fu, deputy commissioner of Shuofang and Left Jinwuwei Grand General, was appointed to inherit the titles of Protector-General of Changle, King of Qinghai, and Wudiyebaledou Khan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，其封襲遂絕。

translations.literal: Before long he died, and the enfeoffment and inheritance then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, and the hereditary titles lapsed.

sentences.zh: 葉谷渾自晉永嘉之末，始西渡洮水，建國於群羌之故地，至為吐蕃所滅，凡三百五十年。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun from the end of the Yongjia era of Jin first crossed west over the Tao River and established a state in the old lands of the various Qiang; until being destroyed by Tibet, altogether three hundred and fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun first crossed the Tao River westward at the end of the Jin Yongjia era and founded a state in the old Qiang territories; from that beginning until Tibet destroyed them, the kingdom lasted three hundred and fifty years.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國焉耆國，在京師西四千三百里，東接高昌，西鄰龜茲，即漢時故地。

translations.literal: The state of Yanqi, the state of Yanqi, is four thousand three hundred li west of the capital; east it adjoins Gaochang, west it borders Kucha—the old territory of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Yanqi lies four thousand three hundred li west of the capital, bordered by Gaochang on the east and Kucha on the west—the same lands known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍氏，名突騎支。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Long; his name is Tuqizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belongs to the Long clan; his name is Tuqizhi.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千餘人，常役屬於西突厥。

translations.literal: Effective troops number more than two thousand men; they are constantly subject and attached to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: It could field a little over two thousand soldiers and usually served the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 其地良沃，多蒲萄，頗有魚鹽之利，

translations.literal: Its land is fertile and rich; grapes are abundant, and there is considerable profit from fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: The land is fertile and rich in grapes, with good profits from fishing and salt.

sentences.zh: 突騎支遣使貢方物，復請開大磧路以便行李，太宗許之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, Tuqizhi sent envoys presenting local products and again requested opening the great desert route to facilitate baggage and travel; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, Tuqizhi sent tribute and again asked that the great desert road be reopened for travelers; Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 自隋末罹亂，磧路遂閉，西域朝貢者皆由高昌。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil at the end of Sui, the desert route was then closed, and Western Region tribute-bearers all went by way of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of the Sui, the desert route had been closed and envoys from the Western Regions all traveled through Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 及是，高昌大怒，遂與焉耆結怨，遣兵襲焉耆，大掠而去。

translations.literal: When this happened, Gaochang was greatly angered, then bore a grudge with Yanqi, sent troops to raid Yanqi, and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang was furious and turned against Yanqi, sending troops to raid the kingdom and withdraw with heavy spoils.

sentences.zh: 西突厥莫賀設與咄陸、弩失畢不協，奔於焉耆，咄陸復來攻之。

translations.literal: Western Turk Moheshe was at odds with Zhulu and Nushibi, fled to Yanqi, and Zhulu again came to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Moheshe of the Western Turks fell out with Zhulu and Nushibi, fled to Yanqi, and Zhulu attacked Yanqi again.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣使言狀，並貢名馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, envoys were sent to report the situation and also present famous horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Yanqi sent envoys to report its situation and presented fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 時西突厥國亂，太宗遣中郎將桑孝彥領左右胄曹韋弘機往安撫之，仍冊立咥利失可汗。

translations.literal: At the time the Western Turk state was in disorder; Taizong sent Palace Gentleman Sang Xiaoyan leading Left and Right Armorer Clerk Wei Hongji to go and pacify them, and still invested and installed Xielishi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: While the Western Turks were in turmoil, Taizong sent Palace Gentleman Sang Xiaoyan with Armorer Clerk Wei Hongji to pacify them and invested Xielishi as khan.

sentences.zh: 可汗既立，素善焉耆，令與焉耆為援。

translations.literal: Once the khan was installed, being by nature on good terms with Yanqi, he ordered that they be mutual support with Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the khan, who had long been friendly with Yanqi, made Yanqi his ally.

sentences.zh: 十二年，處月、處密與高昌攻陷焉耆五城，掠男女一千五百人，焚其廬舍而去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Chuyue and Chumi together with Gaochang attacked and captured five cities of Yanqi, carried off one thousand five hundred men and women, burned their dwellings, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Chuyue and Chumi joined Gaochang in capturing five Yanqi cities, carrying off fifteen hundred people and burning the settlements before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，侯君集討高昌，遣使與之相結，焉耆王大喜，請為聲援。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Hou Junji campaigned against Gaochang; he sent envoys to join with them in alliance; the Yanqi king was greatly pleased and requested to serve as vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Hou Junji marched against Gaochang, he sent envoys to ally with Yanqi; the Yanqi king gladly offered support.

sentences.zh: 及破高昌，其王詣軍門稱謁。

translations.literal: When Gaochang was broken, the Yanqi king came to the army gate to pay respects and audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaochang fell, the Yanqi king came to Hou Junji's camp to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 焉耆人先為高昌所虜者，悉歸之。

translations.literal: Yanqi people who had earlier been captured by Gaochang were all returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: All Yanqi captives held by Gaochang were returned.

sentences.zh: 由是遣使謝恩，並貢方物。

translations.literal: On this account envoys were sent to thank for grace and also present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi then sent envoys to express gratitude and present tribute.

sentences.zh: 其年，西突厥重臣屈利啜為其弟娶焉耆王女，由是相為脣齒，朝貢遂闕。

translations.literal: That year, Western Turk great minister Qulichuo had his younger brother marry the Yanqi king's daughter; on this account they became mutual lips and teeth, and tribute missions then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Western Turk magnate Qulichuo had his brother marry the Yanqi king's daughter; the two realms became close allies, and Yanqi stopped sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪請擊之，太宗許焉。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke requested to attack them; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke asked permission to attack Yanqi, and Taizong approved.

sentences.zh: 會焉耆王弟頡鼻葉護兄弟三人來至西州，孝恪選步騎三千出銀山道，以頡鼻弟栗婆準為鄉導。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yanqi king's younger brother Ji'e Yehu and his three brothers came to Xizhou; Xiaoke selected three thousand infantry and cavalry to set out by the Yinshan route, with Ji'e's younger brother Lipozhun as local guide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yanqi king's brother Ji'e Yehu and two siblings arrived at Xizhou, Xiaoke chose three thousand foot and horse soldiers to advance by the Yinshan route, with Ji'e's brother Lipozhun as guide.

sentences.zh: 焉耆所都城，四面有水，自恃險固，不虞於我。

translations.literal: The city where Yanqi was based had water on all four sides; relying on its perilous solidity, they did not expect us.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi's capital was ringed by water on every side; trusting in its natural defenses, the city did not expect an attack.

sentences.zh: 孝恪倍道兼行，夜至城下，潛遣將士浮水而渡。

translations.literal: Xiaoke doubled the road and marched together, reached below the city by night, and secretly sent officers and soldiers to float across the water and cross.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke forced the march and arrived at the city by night, secretly sending his men to swim across the water.

sentences.zh: 至曉，一時攀堞，鼓角齊震，城中大擾。

translations.literal: By dawn, all at once they climbed the battlements; drums and horns shook together, and great disturbance arose in the city.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they scaled the walls at once; drums and horns sounded together and the city fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 孝恪縱兵擊之，虜其王突騎支，首虜千餘級。

translations.literal: Xiaoke released troops to attack them, captured their king Tuqizhi, and heads and captives numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke unleashed his troops, captured King Tuqizhi, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 以栗婆準導軍有功，留攝國事而還。

translations.literal: Because Lipozhun had merit in guiding the army, he was left to administer state affairs temporarily and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lipozhun had guided the army well, Xiaoke left him in charge of affairs and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時駕幸洛陽宮，孝恪鎖突騎支並其妻子送行在所，詔宥之。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was visiting Luoyang Palace; Xiaoke shackled Tuqizhi together with his wife and children and sent them to the traveling residence; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Luoyang Palace; Xiaoke sent Tuqizhi in chains with his family to the imperial residence, and an edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥屈利啜將兵來援焉耆，孝恪還師三日，屈利啜乃囚栗婆準，而西突厥處般啜令其吐屯來攝焉耆，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Initially, Western Turk Qulichuo was leading troops to aid Yanqi; three days after Xiaoke returned his army, Qulichuo then imprisoned Lipozhun, while Western Turk Chubanchuo ordered his tutun to come and administer Yanqi, and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Western Turk Qulichuo had been marching to relieve Yanqi; three days after Xiaoke withdrew, Qulichuo imprisoned Lipozhun, and Chubanchuo of the Western Turks sent his officer Tutun to take control of Yanqi and dispatch tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 太宗數之曰：「焉耆者，我兵擊得，汝何人，輒來統攝。」

translations.literal: Taizong rebuked him, saying: "Yanqi was taken by our troops in attack—who are you to come presumptuously and administer it?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked him: "We took Yanqi by force—who are you to come and rule it?

sentences.zh: 吐屯懼而返國。

translations.literal: Tutun feared and returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Tutun, frightened, returned home.

sentences.zh: 焉耆又立栗婆準從父兄薛婆阿那支為王。

translations.literal: Yanqi again installed Lipozhun's father's younger brother's son Xuepo Anazhi as king.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi then enthroned Lipozhun's cousin Xuepo Anazhi as king.

sentences.zh: 處般啜乃執栗婆準送於龜茲，為所殺。

translations.literal: Chubanchuo then seized Lipozhun and sent him to Kucha, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chubanchuo seized Lipozhun and sent him to Kucha, where he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 薛婆阿那支既得處般啜為援，遂有國。

translations.literal: Xuepo Anazhi, having obtained Chubanchuo as support, then held the state.
translations.idiomatic: With Chubanchuo's backing, Xuepo Anazhi secured the throne.

sentences.zh: 及阿史那社爾之討龜茲，阿那支大懼，遂奔龜茲，保其東城，以禦官軍。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er campaigned against Kucha, Anazhi was greatly afraid; he then fled to Kucha, defended its eastern city, and resisted the official army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina She'er marched against Kucha, Anazhi fled there in terror, held the eastern city, and tried to resist the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 社爾擊擒之，數其罪而斬焉。

translations.literal: She'er attacked and captured him, enumerated his crimes, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: She'er captured him, recited his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 求得阿那支從父弟先那準，立為王，以修職貢。

translations.literal: They sought and obtained Anazhi's father's younger brother's son Xiannazhun, installed him as king, to restore official tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: They found Anazhi's cousin Xiannazhun, enthroned him, and restored regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 及太宗葬昭陵。

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling,

sentences.zh: 乃刻石像龍突騎支之形，列於玄闕之下。

translations.literal: Then a stone was carved in the likeness of Long Tuqizhi and arrayed below the Dark Gate.
translations.idiomatic: a stone image of Long Tuqizhi was carved and placed among the figures below the Dark Gate.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: From this tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yanqi sent tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國龜茲國，即漢西域舊地也。

translations.literal: The state of Kucha, the state of Kucha, is precisely the old territory of the Western Regions in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Kucha occupied the same Western Region territory known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 在京師西七千五百里。

translations.literal: It is seven thousand five hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven thousand five hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白氏。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Bai.
translations.idiomatic: The royal clan was the Bai.

sentences.zh: 有城郭屋宇，耕田畜牧為業。

translations.literal: There are walled cities and houses; farming fields and raising livestock are their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in walled towns and houses, farming and raising livestock.

sentences.zh: 男女皆翦髮，垂與項齊，唯王不翦髮。

translations.literal: Men and women all cut their hair; it hangs level with the nape, only the king does not cut his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wore their hair cut short, hanging level with the nape; only the king kept his long.

sentences.zh: 學胡書及婆羅門書、算計之事，尤重佛法。

translations.literal: They study Hu script and Brahmin script and matters of calculation; they especially esteem Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: They studied Kuchean and Brahmi scripts and arithmetic, and held the Buddhist faith in especial regard.

sentences.zh: 其王以錦蒙項，著錦袍金寶帶，坐金獅子床。

translations.literal: Its king covers his neck with brocade, wears a brocade robe with golden treasure belt, and sits on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore brocade about his neck, a brocade robe with a gold-studded belt, and sat upon a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 有良馬、封牛。

translations.literal: There are fine horses and humped cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded fine horses and humped cattle.

sentences.zh: 饒蒲萄酒，富室至數百碩。

translations.literal: Rich in grape wine; wealthy households store up to several hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was plentiful; the wealthiest households kept stores of several hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，其主蘇伐勃駃遣使來朝。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, its ruler Subo Bolijiao sent envoys to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu came to the throne, the lord Subo Bolijiao sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 勃駃尋卒，子蘇伐疊代立，號時健莫賀俟利發，

translations.literal: Bolijiao soon died; his son Subo Die succeeded, taking the title Shijian Mohe Shilifa.
translations.idiomatic: Bolijiao soon died and was succeeded by his son Subo Die, who took the title Shijian Mohe Shilifa.

sentences.zh: 又遣使獻馬，太宗賜以璽書，撫慰甚厚，由此歲貢不絕，然臣於西突厥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, he again sent envoys presenting horses; Taizong granted an imperial missive sealed with the seal, with exceedingly generous assurances; from this annual tribute never ceased, yet he remained subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan (630), he again sent envoys with horses. Taizong answered with an imperial letter and generous reassurance, and yearly tribute thereafter never lapsed—though Kucha remained a vassal of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪來伐焉耆，龜茲遣兵援助，自是職貢頗闕。

translations.literal: When Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoke came to attack Yanqi, Kucha sent troops to aid them; from this tribute duties were largely absent.
translations.idiomatic: When Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoke marched against Yanqi, Kucha sent troops to its aid, and from then on tribute fell largely into abeyance.

sentences.zh: 伐疊死，其弟訶黎布失畢代立，漸失籓臣禮。

translations.literal: Die died; his younger brother Heli Bushibi succeeded in his place, gradually losing the observances due a vassal prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Die died, his younger brother Heli Bushibi took the throne and gradually abandoned the courtesies owed to the Celestial Court.

sentences.zh: 二十年，太宗遣左驍衛大將軍阿史那社爾為昆山道行軍大總管，與安西都護郭孝恪、司農卿楊弘禮率五將軍，又發鐵勒十三部兵十餘萬騎，以伐龜茲。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Taizong dispatched Left Xiaowei Grand General Ashina She'er as Commander-in-Chief of the Kunshan Route Army, together with Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoke and Minister of Public Works Yang Hongli leading five generals, also raising more than a hundred thousand cavalry from the thirteen tribes of the Tiele, to attack Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan (646), Taizong appointed Left Xiaowei Grand General Ashina She'er overall commander of the Kunshan expedition, joined by Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoke, Minister of Public Works Yang Hongli, and five other generals. More than a hundred thousand Tiele cavalry were mobilized for the assault on Kucha.

sentences.zh: 社爾既破西蕃處月、處密，乃進師趨其北境，出其不意，西突厥所署焉耆王棄城而遁，社爾遣輕騎追擒之。

translations.literal: After She'er had defeated the Western Barbarians Chuyue and Chumi, he then advanced his army toward their northern borderlands; catching them unawares, the Yanqi king appointed by the Western Turks abandoned the city and fled; She'er sent light cavalry in pursuit and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing the Chuyue and Chumi tribes in the west, She'er pressed north into Kuchean territory. Taken by surprise, the Yanqi king installed by the Western Turks fled his city; She'er's light cavalry ran him down and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 龜茲大震，守將多棄城而走。

translations.literal: Kucha was greatly shaken; garrison commanders mostly abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was thrown into panic, and many garrison commanders abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 社爾進屯積石，去其都城三百里。

translations.literal: She'er advanced and encamped at Jishi, three hundred li from their capital city.
translations.idiomatic: She'er advanced to Jishi, three hundred li from the Kuchean capital.

sentences.zh: 遣伊州刺史韓威率千餘騎為前鋒，右驍衛將軍曹繼叔次之。

translations.literal: He sent Yizhou Prefect Han Wei leading more than a thousand cavalry as vanguard; Right Xiaowei General Cao Jishu followed after.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei, prefect of Yizhou, led a thousand cavalry as vanguard, with Right Xiaowei General Cao Jishu following in support.

sentences.zh: 西至多褐城，與龜茲王相遇，及其相那利、將羯獵顛等，有眾五萬，逆拒王師。

translations.literal: Proceeding west to Duohu City, they encountered the King of Kucha, together with his chancellor Nali, the general Jieliedian, and others, with a force of fifty thousand, who met the imperial army in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: West of Duohu City they met the Kuchean king, his chancellor Nali, General Jieliedian, and some fifty thousand troops who barred the imperial army's path.

sentences.zh: 威乃偽遁而引之，其王俟利發見威兵少，悉眾而至。

translations.literal: Han Wei feigned retreat to lure them; the king Shilifa, seeing Wei's forces were few, came forth with his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei feigned retreat to draw them on. King Shilifa, seeing how few his troops were, brought out his full strength.

sentences.zh: 威退行三十里，與繼叔軍會，合擊大破之。

translations.literal: Wei withdrew thirty li and joined with Jishu's army; together they struck and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei pulled back thirty li, linked up with Cao Jishu's force, and together they delivered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 其王退保都城，社爾進軍逼之，王乃輕騎而走，遂下其城，令孝恪守之。

translations.literal: The king withdrew to hold the capital city; She'er advanced his army pressing upon him; the king then fled with light cavalry; they thereupon took the city and ordered Xiaoke to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The king fell back on his capital; She'er pressed the siege. The king escaped with a light escort, the city fell, and Guo Xiaoke was left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 遣沙州刺史蘇海政、尚輦奉禦薛萬備以精騎逼之，行六百里，其王窘急，退保於撥換城。

translations.literal: He dispatched Shazhou Prefect Su Haizheng and Palace Attendant Xue Wanbei with elite cavalry pressing upon him; traveling six hundred li, the king, pressed to desperation, withdrew to hold Bochuan City.
translations.idiomatic: Su Haizheng, prefect of Shazhou, and Palace Attendant Xue Wanbei chased him six hundred li with elite cavalry until the king, in desperate straits, took refuge in Bochuan Fortress.

sentences.zh: 社爾等進軍圍之，擒其王及大將羯獵顛等。

translations.literal: She'er and the others advanced their army and besieged it, capturing the king and the great general Jieliedian and others.
translations.idiomatic: She'er besieged the fortress and captured the king, General Jieliedian, and others.

sentences.zh: 其相那利僅以身免，潛引西突厥之眾並其國兵萬餘人，來襲孝恪，殺之，官軍大擾。

translations.literal: His chancellor Nali alone escaped with his body intact; secretly he brought Western Turk forces together with more than ten thousand of his country's troops to attack Xiaoke, killing him; the official army fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Nali alone escaped. Secretly rallying Western Turk allies and more than ten thousand Kucheans, he fell upon Guo Xiaoke and killed him, throwing the Tang forces into chaos.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中崔義起與曹繼叔、韓威等擊之，那利敗走。

translations.literal: Secretariat Section Chief Cui Yiqi together with Cao Jishu, Han Wei, and others attacked them; Nali was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yiqi of the Secretariat, together with Cao Jishu and Han Wei, counterattacked and drove Nali from the field.

sentences.zh: 尋為龜茲人所執以詣軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was seized by men of Kucha and brought before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kucheans seized him and delivered him to the Tang camp.

sentences.zh: 前後破其大城五所，虜男女數萬口。

translations.literal: Before and after, they broke five of their great cities and took captive men and women numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In all, five great cities were taken and tens of thousands of people carried off.

sentences.zh: 社爾因立其王之弟葉護為王，勒石紀功而旋。

translations.literal: She'er thereupon established the king's younger brother Yehu as king, carved stone to record the achievement, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: She'er installed the king's brother Yehu as ruler, erected a victory stele, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俘其王訶黎布失畢及那利、羯獵顛等獻於社廟。

translations.literal: The captured king Heli Bushibi together with Nali, Jieliedian, and others were presented at the Temple of Earth and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Heli Bushibi, Nali, Jieliedian, and the other prisoners were presented at the imperial shrine.

sentences.zh: 尋以訶黎布失畢為左武翊衛中郎將，那利已下授官各有差。

translations.literal: Soon Heli Bushibi was made Middle General of the Left Wuyi Guard; those from Nali downward were bestowed offices each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Heli Bushibi was soon appointed Middle General of the Left Wuyi Guard, while Nali and the others received offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗之葬昭陵，乃刻石像其形，列於玄闕之前，

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone was carved in his likeness and arrayed before the Dark Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was laid to rest at Zhaoling, stone images of the captives were carved and set before the Dark Gate of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 又以訶黎布失畢為右驍衛大將軍，尋放還蕃，撫其餘眾，依舊為龜茲王，賜物一千段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, Heli Bushibi was again made Right Xiaowei Grand General; soon he was released and returned to his realm, comforting the remaining people, continuing as before as King of Kucha, and was granted a thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui (650), Heli Bushibi was again made Right Xiaowei Grand General, then released to his kingdom to reassure the people and resume rule as King of Kucha, with a gift of a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗既破龜茲，移置安西都護府於其國城，以郭孝恪為都護，兼統於闐、疏勒、碎葉，謂之「四鎮」。

translations.literal: Previously, after Taizong had defeated Kucha, he moved and established the Anxi Protectorate in its capital city, appointing Guo Xiaoke as protector, simultaneously administering Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab, called the "Four Garrisons."
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's conquest of Kucha, the Anxi Protectorate was moved to the Kuchean capital. Guo Xiaoke was named protector over Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab as well—the Four Garrisons of the west.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，不欲廣地勞人，復命有司棄龜茲等四鎮，移安西依舊於西州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, not wishing to extend territory and exhaust the people, he again ordered the officials to abandon Kucha and the other four garrisons and move Anxi back as before to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong, unwilling to overextend the realm and burden the people, ordered the Four Garrisons including Kucha abandoned and the Anxi Protectorate returned to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃大入，焉耆已西四鎮城堡，並為賊所陷。

translations.literal: Afterward the Tibetans entered on a great scale; the four garrisons' castles west of Yanqi were all seized by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tibet invaded in force, and the four garrisons west of Yanqi fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，，武威軍總管王孝傑、阿史那忠節大破吐蕃，克復龜茲、於闐等四鎮，自此復於龜茲置安西都護府，用漢兵三萬人以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, in the first year of Changshou, Wuwei Army Supervisor Wang Xiaojie and Ashina Zhongjie greatly defeated the Tibetans, recaptured Kucha, Khotan, and the other four garrisons; from this they again established the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha, using thirty thousand Han troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu's regency, Wang Xiaojie and Ashina Zhongjie crushed the Tibetans in the first year of Changshou (692) and recovered the Four Garrisons including Kucha and Khotan. The Anxi Protectorate was re-established at Kuche, garrisoned by thirty thousand Han soldiers.

sentences.zh: 既征發內地精兵，遠逾沙磧。

translations.literal: Having conscripted elite troops from the interior, they crossed far beyond the sand deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops were conscripted from the interior and sent far across the deserts.

sentences.zh: 並資遣衣糧等，甚為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: Together with provisions of clothing and grain and the like, this greatly afflicted the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The clothing, grain, and transport levies inflicted great hardship on the people.

sentences.zh: 言事者多請棄之，則天竟不許。

translations.literal: Those who remonstrated mostly asked to abandon them; Zetian ultimately did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists urged abandonment of the garrisons, but Empress Wu would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 其安西都護，則天時有田揚名，中宗時有郭元振，開元初則張孝暠、杜暹，皆有政績，為夷人所伏。

translations.literal: Among the Anxi Protectors, in Zetian's time there was Tian Yangming; in Zhongzong's time Guo Yuanzhen; at the beginning of Kaiyuan Zhang Xiaogao and Du Xian—all had achievements in governance and were respected by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi protectorship produced able administrators—Tian Yangming under Wu, Guo Yuanzhen under Zhongzong, Zhang Xiaogao and Du Xian in the early Kaiyuan era—each esteemed by the western peoples.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國疏勒國，即漢時舊地也。

translations.literal: The state of Kashgar, the state of Kashgar, is precisely the old territory of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar occupied the same territory known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 西帶蔥嶺，在京師西九千三百里。

translations.literal: To the west it borders the Pamirs; it is nine thousand three hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered the Pamirs to the west, lying nine thousand three hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其王姓裴氏。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The royal clan was the Pei.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，突厥以女妻王。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, the Turks gave a daughter in marriage to the king.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, the Turks gave a princess in marriage to the Kashgar king.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Available troops two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 俗事祅神，有胡書文字，

translations.literal: By custom they serve the fire god; they have Hu script and writing.
translations.idiomatic: The people worshipped the fire god and used a script of their own.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻名馬，自是朝貢不絕，

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys presenting famous horses; from this tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan (635), envoys brought celebrated horses, and tribute thereafter continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣使冊立其王裴安定為疏勒王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong sent envoys to invest his king Pei Anding as King of Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan (728), Xuanzong invested King Pei Anding as ruler of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 于闐國于闐國，西南帶蔥嶺，與龜茲接，在京師西九千七百里。

translations.literal: The state of Khotan, the state of Khotan, to the southwest borders the Pamirs, adjoins Kucha, and is nine thousand seven hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan, southwest of the Pamirs and bordering Kucha, lay nine thousand seven hundred li west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 勝兵四千人。

translations.literal: Available troops four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 其國出美玉。

translations.literal: That country produces fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The land was famed for fine jade.

sentences.zh: 俗多機巧，好事祅神，崇佛教。

translations.literal: By custom they are much skilled and ingenious; they favor serving the fire god and revere Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: The people were ingenious by nature, worshipped the fire god, and held Buddhism in high regard.

sentences.zh: 先臣於西突厥。

translations.literal: Formerly they were subjects of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: They had formerly been vassals of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 其王姓尉遲氏，名屈密，

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Yuchi; his name is Qumi.
translations.idiomatic: The king, of the Yuchi clan, was named Qumi.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻玉帶，太宗優詔答之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys presenting a jade belt; Taizong answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan (632), envoys brought a jade belt, which Taizong acknowledged with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, they again sent a son to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (639), a princely son was again sent to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 及阿史那社爾伐龜茲，其王伏闍信大懼，使其子以駝萬三百匹饋軍。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er attacked Kucha, its king Fuxinxin was greatly afraid and sent his son with thirteen thousand camels to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina She'er marched on Kucha, King Fuxinxin was terrified and sent his son with thirteen thousand camels to supply the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 及將旋師，行軍長史薛萬備請社爾曰：「今者既破龜茲，國威已振，請因此機，願以輕騎羈取于闐之王。」

translations.literal: When about to withdraw the army, Campaign Chief Clerk Xue Wanbei asked She'er, saying: "Now that we have already defeated Kucha and the nation's prestige is already shaken, I beg to take advantage of this opportunity and wish with light cavalry to seize the King of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: As the army prepared to withdraw, Chief Clerk Xue Wanbei urged She'er: "Kucha is broken and imperial prestige stands high. Grant me light cavalry, and I will bring the King of Khotan in.

sentences.zh: 社爾乃遣萬備率五十騎抵于闐之國，萬備陳國威靈，勸其入見天子，伏闍信於是隨萬備來朝。

translations.literal: She'er thereupon sent Wanbei leading fifty horsemen to reach the state of Khotan; Wanbei set forth the nation's prestige and authority and urged him to come in person to see the Son of Heaven; Fuxinxin thereupon followed Wanbei to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: She'er dispatched Wanbei with fifty riders to Khotan. Wanbei displayed the empire's might and urged the king to appear before the Son of Heaven. Fuxinxin thereupon accompanied him to court.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，拜右驍衛大將軍，又授其子葉護玷為右驍衛將軍，並賜金帶、錦袍、布帛六十段，並宅一區，留數月而遣之，因請留子弟以宿衛。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he invested him as Right Xiaowei Grand General, further appointed his son Yehudian as Right Xiaowei General, together bestowing golden belt, brocade robe, sixty rolls of cloth and silk, and one residential compound; he was retained several months then dispatched; thereupon he requested to leave younger kinsmen to serve as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong invested him as Right Xiaowei Grand General and appointed his son Yehudian Right Xiaowei General, with a gold belt, brocade robe, sixty bolts of silk, and a residence in the capital. After several months at court he was dismissed, but he asked that younger relatives remain behind as imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 太宗葬昭陵，刻石像其形，列於玄闕之下，

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone was carved in his likeness and arrayed below the Dark Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's burial at Zhaoling, his stone image was carved and placed below the Dark Gate.

sentences.zh: 其王伏闍雄復來入朝，

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong, its king Fuxinxiong again came to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuigong (687), King Fuxinxiong again came to court.

sentences.zh: 伏闍雄卒，則天封其子璥為于闐國王，

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshou, Fuxinxiong died; Zetian enfeoffed his son Jun as King of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxinxiong died in the third year of Tianshou (692); Empress Wu invested his son Jun as King of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 復冊立尉遲伏師為于闐王，數遣使朝貢，

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, she again invested Yuchi Fushi as King of Khotan; repeatedly envoys were sent to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan (728), Yuchi Fushi was again invested as King of Khotan, and tribute missions followed in number.

sentences.zh: 以于闐王尉遲勝弟守左監門衛率葉護曜為太僕員外卿，仍同四鎮節度副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan, Yehuyao, younger brother of Khotan King Yuchi Sheng and Commandant of the Left Jianmen Guard, was made Outer Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and simultaneously Associate Four Garrisons Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyuan (760), Yuchi Sheng's brother Yehuyao—commandant of the Left Jianmen Guard—was appointed Outer Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and deputy commissioner of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 權知本國事。

translations.literal: Acting in authority over affairs of his own country.
translations.idiomatic: He was given provisional authority over Khotan's affairs.

sentences.zh: 以勝至德初領兵赴國難，因堅請留宿衛，故有是命，事有勝傳。

translations.literal: Because Sheng at the beginning of Zhide led troops to answer the nation's crisis, and thereupon firmly requested to remain as palace guard, therefore this appointment was made; the matter is recorded in Sheng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sheng had marched to the capital's defense at the start of the Zhide era and pleaded to remain as a palace guard, this arrangement was made; the full account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 天竺國天竺國，即漢之身毒國，或云婆羅門地也。

translations.literal: The state of Tianzhu, the state of Tianzhu, is precisely the Shendu state of Han, or it is said to be the land of the Brahmins.
translations.idiomatic: India—known in Han times as Shendu, also called the land of the Brahmins.

sentences.zh: 在葱嶺，周三萬餘里。

translations.literal: It lies at the Pamirs; its circumference is more than thirty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay beyond the Pamirs, measuring more than thirty thousand li around its perimeter.

sentences.zh: 其中分為五天竺：其一曰中天竺，二曰東天竺，三曰南天竺，四曰西天竺，五曰北天竺。

translations.literal: Within it is divided into five Tianzhu: the first is called Central Tianzhu, the second Eastern Tianzhu, the third Southern Tianzhu, the fourth Western Tianzhu, the fifth Northern Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Within its bounds lay five Indias: Central, Eastern, Southern, Western, and Northern.

sentences.zh: 地各數千里，城邑數百。

translations.literal: Each territory extends several thousand li; cities and towns number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Each region stretched thousands of li, with hundreds of cities and towns.

sentences.zh: 南天竺際大海，北天竺拒雪山，四周有山為壁，南面一谷，通為國門；

translations.literal: Southern Tianzhu borders the great sea; Northern Tianzhu faces the snow mountains; on all four sides mountains form ramparts; one valley to the south serves as the gate of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Southern India faced the ocean; Northern India abutted the snow peaks. Mountains ringed the land like walls, with a single southern valley serving as the national gate.

sentences.zh: 東天竺東際大海，與扶南、林邑鄰接；

translations.literal: Eastern Tianzhu eastward borders the great sea, adjoining Funan and Linyi;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern India touched the sea and bordered Funan and Linyi;

sentences.zh: 西天竺與罽賓、波斯相接；

translations.literal: Western Tianzhu adjoins Jibin and Persia;
translations.idiomatic: Western India met Jibin and Persia;

sentences.zh: 中天竺據四天竺之會，其都城週迴七十餘里，北臨禪連河。

translations.literal: Central Tianzhu occupies the juncture of the four Tianzhu; its capital city has a circumference of more than seventy li, facing north upon the Chanlian River.
translations.idiomatic: Central India occupied the crossroads of the four regions. Its capital measured more than seventy li around and stood north upon the Ganges.

sentences.zh: 云昔有婆羅門領徒千人，肄業於樹下，樹神降之，遂為夫婦。

translations.literal: It is said that long ago a Brahmin led a thousand disciples studying under a tree; the tree spirit descended upon him, and they became husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Legend held that a Brahmin once led a thousand disciples in study beneath a sacred tree. A tree spirit descended to him, and the two became man and wife.

sentences.zh: 宮室自然而立，僮僕甚盛。

translations.literal: Palace halls arose of themselves; servants and attendants were exceedingly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: A palace sprang up of its own accord, attended by a vast retinue of servants.

sentences.zh: 於是使役百神，築城以統之，經日而就。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made the hundred spirits serve him, building a city to rule over them; in the course of a day it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded the spirits to build a city in a single day to rule over them.

sentences.zh: 此後有阿育王，復役使鬼神，累石為宮闕，皆雕文刻鏤。

translations.literal: After this there was King Ashoka, who again compelled ghosts and spirits; piling stone he made palace halls, all carved with ornamental design and filigree.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Ashoka likewise conscripted supernatural laborers to pile stones into palaces richly carved and ornamented.

sentences.zh: 非人力所及。

translations.literal: Beyond what human strength can achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Works beyond human power to accomplish.

sentences.zh: 阿育王頗行苛政，置砲烙之刑，謂之地獄，今城中見有其跡焉。

translations.literal: King Ashoka rather practiced harsh governance, establishing the punishment of the burning pillar, called hell; today within the city one can still see traces of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ashoka ruled harshly, instituting a burning-pillar torture he called "hell"; traces of it may still be seen in the capital.

sentences.zh: 中天竺王姓乞利咥氏，或云刹利氏，世有其國，不相篡弒。

translations.literal: The King of Central Tianzhu bears the surname Qilizhi, or it is said the Kshatriya clan; generation after generation they hold their state; they do not usurp or assassinate one another.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Central India were of the Kshatriya line, or the Qilizhi clan, holding sovereign power from generation to generation without usurpation or regicide.

sentences.zh: 厥土卑濕暑熱，稻歲四熟，有金剛，似紫石英，百煉不銷，可以切玉。

translations.literal: That land is low, damp, and sweltering hot; rice ripens four times a year; there is diamond, resembling purple crystal quartz; refined a hundred times it does not melt away; it can cut jade.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low, damp, and torrid, yielding four rice harvests a year. There was a stone like amethyst, called diamond—untouched by fire and hard enough to cut jade.

sentences.zh: 又有旃檀、鬱金諸香。

translations.literal: Moreover there are sandalwood, turmeric, and various aromatics.
translations.idiomatic: Sandalwood, saffron, and other fragrant substances grew there as well.

sentences.zh: 通於大秦，故其寶物或至扶南、交趾貿易焉。

translations.literal: It communicates with Daqin; therefore its precious goods sometimes reach Funan and Jiaozhi for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Trade reached as far as Rome, and Indian goods found their way to markets in Funan and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 百姓殷樂，俗無簿籍，耕王地者輸地利。

translations.literal: The common people are prosperous and contented; by custom there are no household registers; those who cultivate royal lands render the land's yield.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in prosperity. There were no household registers; farmers on crown lands paid a share of the harvest.

sentences.zh: 以齒貝為貨。

translations.literal: They use cowrie shells as currency.
translations.idiomatic: Cowrie shells served as currency.

sentences.zh: 人皆深目長鼻。

translations.literal: The people all have deep-set eyes and long noses.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes and prominent noses.

sentences.zh: 致敬極者，舐足摩踵。

translations.literal: Those who show utmost reverence lick the feet and rub the heels.
translations.idiomatic: The highest form of obeisance was to lick the feet and press upon the heels.

sentences.zh: 家有奇樂倡伎。

translations.literal: Every household has remarkable music and singing courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: Every household kept musicians and dancers of rare skill.

sentences.zh: 其王與大臣多服錦罽。

translations.literal: The king and great ministers mostly wear brocade and felt rugs.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his ministers commonly wore brocade and felt.

sentences.zh: 上為螺髻於頂，餘髮翦之使拳。

translations.literal: On top they wear snail-shell topknots on the crown; the remaining hair is cut short and made into fists.
translations.idiomatic: They wore coiled topknots on the crown, with the rest of the hair cropped short.

sentences.zh: 俗皆徒跣。

translations.literal: By custom all go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: All went barefoot by custom.

sentences.zh: 衣重白色，唯梵志種姓披白疊以為異。

translations.literal: Clothing favors white color; only the Brahmin caste wears white cotton cloth as their distinction.
translations.idiomatic: White was the favored color, but only Brahmins wore white cotton as a mark of their caste.

sentences.zh: 死者或焚屍取灰，以為浮圖；

translations.literal: For the dead, some burn the corpse and take the ashes to make a stupa;
translations.idiomatic: Some burned the dead and built stupas from the ashes;

sentences.zh: 或委之中野，以施禽獸；

translations.literal: some cast them in the wild to feed birds and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: some left corpses in the open for birds and beasts;

sentences.zh: 或流之於河，以飼魚鼈。

translations.literal: some cast them into rivers to feed fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: some cast them into rivers for fish and turtles.

sentences.zh: 無喪紀之文。

translations.literal: There are no mourning rites written down.
translations.idiomatic: No written codes governed funeral observances.

sentences.zh: 謀反者幽殺之，小犯罰錢以贖罪。

translations.literal: Those who plot rebellion are secretly put to death; minor offenses are fined money to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Treason was punished by secret execution; lesser offenses by fines.

sentences.zh: 不孝則斷手刖足，截耳割鼻，放流邊外。

translations.literal: For unfilial conduct hands are severed and feet cut off, ears cut and noses sliced, and one is exiled beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Filial impiety brought amputation of hands or feet, mutilation of ears or nose, and exile beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 有文字，善天文算曆之術。

translations.literal: They have writing; they are skilled in the arts of astronomy, calculation, and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed a written script and excelled in astronomy, mathematics, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 其人皆學《悉曇章》，云是梵天法。

translations.literal: The people all study the "Siddham Chapter"; it is said to be the law of Brahma Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: All studied the Siddham script, said to be the sacred law of Brahma.

sentences.zh: 書於貝多樹葉以紀事。

translations.literal: They write upon pattra tree leaves to record affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded matters on leaves of the pattra tree.

sentences.zh: 不殺生飲酒。

translations.literal: They do not kill living beings or drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: They abstained from killing and from wine.

sentences.zh: 國中往往有舊佛跡。

translations.literal: Throughout the country there are often traces of the Buddha from old times.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the land ancient traces of the Buddha could still be found.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，遣裴矩應接西蕃，諸國多有至者，唯天竺不通，帝以為恨。

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Yang of Sui, Pei Ju was sent to receive and entertain the Western Regions; many states came, but only India did not communicate—the emperor regarded this as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang of the Sui, Pei Ju was dispatched to receive envoys from the Western Regions. Many states sent missions, but India alone remained out of contact, and the emperor counted it a grievance.

sentences.zh: 當武德中，其國大亂。

translations.literal: When the Wude era arrived, that country fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign, the country was torn by civil war.

sentences.zh: 其嗣王尸羅逸多練兵聚衆，所向無敵。

translations.literal: The heir-king Shiluoyiduo drilled troops and gathered multitudes; wherever he went none could stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: The heir to the throne, Shiluoyiduo, trained armies and rallied followers until none could withstand him.

sentences.zh: 象不解鞍，人不釋甲，居六載而四天竺之君皆北面以臣之，威勢遠振，刑政甚肅，

translations.literal: Elephants did not leave their saddles, men did not doff their armor; within six years the rulers of the four Indias all turned north to serve him as subjects. His prestige shook distant lands and punishments and government were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Elephants went unsaddled and men slept in their armor. Within six years the kings of the four Indias all turned north to submit as his vassals. His power resounded far abroad, and his justice was stern.

sentences.zh: 尸羅逸多自稱摩伽陀王，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, Shiluoyiduo styled himself King of Magadha and sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan (641), Shiluoyiduo proclaimed himself King of Magadha and dispatched envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗降璽書慰問，尸羅逸多大驚，問諸國人曰：「自古曾有摩訶震旦使人至吾國乎？」

translations.literal: Taizong sent down an imperial edict of inquiry and reassurance. Shiluoyiduo was greatly astonished and asked the people of his state: "From antiquity has there ever been an envoy of Great Mahacina come to our country?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent a sealed edict of greeting and inquiry. Shiluoyiduo was astonished and asked his subjects: "Has an envoy from Great China ever reached our land in all of history?

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「未之有也。」

translations.literal: All said: "There has never been such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Never."

sentences.zh: 乃膜拜而受詔書，因遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He then bowed in worship and received the edict, and thereupon sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself in worship to receive the edict, then sent envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其地遠，禮之甚厚，復遣衛尉丞李義表報使。

translations.literal: Taizong, because the land was distant, treated them with great courtesy and again sent Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yibiao as a return envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Because their land lay so far away, Taizong received them with exceptional honor and sent Li Yibiao of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices back as his envoy.

sentences.zh: 尸羅逸多遣大臣郊迎，傾城邑以縱觀，焚香夾道，逸多率其臣下東面拜受敕書，復遣使獻火珠及鬱金香、菩提樹，

translations.literal: Shiluoyiduo sent high ministers to meet the envoy beyond the suburbs; the whole city poured out to watch. Incense burned along the road. Yiduo led his ministers to bow eastward and receive the imperial letter, and again sent envoys presenting fire pearls, aloeswood, and a bodhi tree.
translations.idiomatic: Shiluoyiduo sent ministers to greet the envoy outside the city, and the whole populace turned out to watch. Incense lined the roads. Yiduo led his court in bowing eastward to receive the imperial letter, then sent tribute of fire pearls, aloeswood, and a bodhi tree.

sentences.zh: 沙門玄奘至其國，將梵本經論六百餘部而歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, the monk Xuanzang reached that country and returned bearing more than six hundred fascicles of Sanskrit sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan (636), the monk Xuanzang reached India and returned with more than six hundred volumes of Sanskrit scriptures and treatises.

sentences.zh: 先是遣右率府長史王玄策使天竺，其四天竺國王咸遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Earlier the Right Rate Office Chief Secretary Wang Xuance had been sent as envoy to India, and the kings of the four Indias all sent envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Xuance, chief secretary of the Right Rate Office, had been sent as envoy to India, and the kings of all four Indias sent missions to court.

sentences.zh: 會中天竺王尸羅逸多死，國中大亂，其臣那伏帝阿羅那順篡立，乃盡發胡兵以拒玄策。

translations.literal: It happened that the king of Central India, Shiluoyiduo, died and the country fell into great disorder. His minister Nafodi Aluanshun usurped the throne and then mustered all foreign troops to resist Xuance.
translations.idiomatic: Just then King Shiluoyiduo of Central India died and the realm descended into chaos. His minister Nafodi Aluanshun seized the throne and raised every foreign soldier he could to oppose Xuance.

sentences.zh: 玄策從騎三十人與胡禦戰，不敵，矢盡，悉被擒。

translations.literal: Xuance, with thirty mounted followers, fought the foreigners but could not prevail; when their arrows were exhausted they were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance and his thirty horsemen fought the invaders but were overwhelmed; when their arrows ran out, all were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 胡並掠諸國貢獻之物。

translations.literal: The foreigners also plundered the tribute goods of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders also looted the tribute brought by the other kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 玄策乃挺身宵遁，走至吐蕃，發精銳一千二百人，並泥婆羅國七千餘騎，以從玄策。

translations.literal: Xuance then slipped away alone by night, fled to Tibet, and raised twelve hundred picked troops, together with more than seven thousand cavalry of Nepal, to follow Xuance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance escaped alone by night, fled to Tibet, and raised twelve hundred elite troops plus more than seven thousand Nepalese cavalry to march with him.

sentences.zh: 玄策與副使蔣師仁率二國兵進至中天竺國城，連戰三日，大破之，斬首三千餘級，赴水溺死者且萬人，阿羅那順棄城而遁，師仁進擒獲之。

translations.literal: Xuance and the vice-envoy Jiang Shiren led the armies of the two states forward to the capital of Central India. They fought for three days straight and won a great victory, beheading more than three thousand and with nearly ten thousand drowned fleeing into the water. Aluanshun abandoned the city and fled; Shiren pressed forward and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance and his deputy Jiang Shiren led the combined armies to the capital of Central India. After three days of battle they routed the enemy, killing more than three thousand and drowning nearly ten thousand in flight. Aluanshun abandoned the city and fled, but Shiren pursued and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 虜男女萬二千人，牛馬三萬餘頭匹。

translations.literal: They captured twelve thousand men and women and more than thirty thousand head of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They took twelve thousand captives and more than thirty thousand head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 於是天竺震懼，俘阿羅那順以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon India trembled in fear, and they carried Aluanshun captive back home.
translations.idiomatic: India was struck with terror, and Aluanshun was brought back as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年至京師，太宗大悅，命有司告宗廟，而謂羣臣曰：「夫人耳目玩於聲色，口鼻耽於臭味，此乃敗德之源。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he reached the capital. Taizong was greatly pleased, ordered the relevant offices to announce it at the ancestral temple, and said to the assembled ministers: "When a person's ears and eyes indulge in sound and color and mouth and nose cling to flavors and scents, this is the source of ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan (648) he reached the capital. Taizong was delighted, ordered the rites announced at the ancestral temple, and told his ministers: "When ears and eyes are given over to music and beauty, and mouth and nose to taste and scent, virtue is undone at the root.

sentences.zh: 若婆羅門不劫掠我使人，豈為俘虜耶？

translations.literal: If the Brahmins had not plundered our envoy, how would they have become captives?
translations.idiomatic: Had the Brahmins not robbed our envoy, would they now be prisoners?

sentences.zh: 昔中山以貪寶取弊，蜀侯以金牛致滅，莫不由之。」

translations.literal: Formerly Zhongshan perished through greed for treasure, and the Lord of Shu was destroyed by the golden ox—never without this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan was ruined by coveting jewels, and the Lord of Shu was destroyed by a golden ox—disaster always begins this way.

sentences.zh: 拜玄策朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Xuance was appointed Gentleman for Promoting Good Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance was appointed Gentleman for Promoting Good Governance.

sentences.zh: 是時就其國得方土那羅邇娑婆寐，自言壽二百歲，云有長生之術。

translations.literal: At that time from that country they obtained the local master Narayanasvami, who declared himself two hundred years old and claimed to possess the art of prolonging life.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they obtained from India a local adept named Narayanasvami, who claimed to be two hundred years old and to know the secret of longevity.

sentences.zh: 太宗深加禮敬，館之於金飈門內。

translations.literal: Taizong treated him with deep courtesy and lodged him within the Jinfeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong honored him lavishly and housed him inside the Jinfeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 造延年之藥。

translations.literal: He prepared a drug to prolong life.
translations.idiomatic: He began preparing an elixir of long life.

sentences.zh: 令兵部尚書崔敦禮監主之，發使天下，採諸奇藥異石，不可稱數。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli to supervise it and sent envoys throughout the empire to gather every rare drug and exotic stone—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong put Minister of War Cui Dunli in charge and sent agents across the empire to collect rare herbs and exotic stones beyond number.

sentences.zh: 延歷歲月，藥成，服竟不效，後放還本國。

translations.literal: Months and years passed; when the drug was finished they took it but it had no effect, and afterward he was sent back to his native country.
translations.idiomatic: Months stretched into years. When the elixir was ready they swallowed it, but it did nothing; afterward he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 太宗之葬昭陵也，刻石像阿羅那順之形，列於玄闕之下。

translations.literal: When Taizong was buried at Zhaoling, a stone image in the likeness of Aluanshun was carved and set beneath the Xuanque.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was laid to rest at Zhaoling, a stone figure of Aluanshun was carved and placed beneath the spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 五天竺所屬之國數十，風俗物產略同。

translations.literal: The states subject to the five Indias number several tens; customs and products are broadly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen states fell under the five Indias; their customs and products were much alike.

sentences.zh: 有伽沒路國，其俗開東門以向日。

translations.literal: There is the state of Kamarupa; its custom is to open the eastern gate toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In Kamarupa the custom was to open the eastern gate to face the rising sun.

sentences.zh: 王玄策至，其王發使貢以奇珍異物及地圖，因請老子像及《道德經》。

translations.literal: When Wang Xuance arrived, its king sent envoys presenting rare treasures and exotic goods and a map, and requested a portrait of Laozi and the Daodejing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xuance arrived, the king sent tribute of rare treasures and a map, and asked for an image of Laozi and a copy of the Daodejing.

sentences.zh: 那揭陀國，有醯羅城，中有重閣，藏佛頂骨及錫杖，

translations.literal: In the state of Nagara there is the city of Hiranyapura; within it is a multi-storied pavilion storing the Buddha's cranial bone and his iron staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Nagara stood the city of Hiranyapura, where a tower housed the Buddha's skull relic and his iron staff.

sentences.zh: 遣使貢方物，

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan (646), envoys were sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 東天竺王摩羅枝摩、西天竺王尸羅逸多、南天竺王遮婁其拔羅婆、北天竺王婁其那那、中天竺王地婆西那，並來朝獻，

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, the kings of East India Moluozimo, West India Shiluoyiduo, South India Zhelouqibaluopo, North India Louqinana, and Central India Dipoxina all came to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou (691), the kings of East, West, South, North, and Central India all came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 南天竺國復遣使來朝，

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong, South India again sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong (710), South India again sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 復遣使貢方物，

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun (710), envoys again brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 西天竺復遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, West India again sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan (714), West India again sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年，南天竺國遣使獻五色能言鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, South India sent envoys presenting a five-colored talking parrot.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan (720), South India sent a five-colored parrot that could speak.

sentences.zh: 其年，南天竺國王尸利那羅僧伽請以戰象及兵馬討大食及吐蕃等，仍求有及名其軍。

translations.literal: That same year, the king of South India Shilinaluosengge requested to use war elephants and troops to attack the Arabs, Tibet, and others, and still asked for an official appointment and to name his army.
translations.idiomatic: That same year King Shilinaluosengge of South India offered war elephants and troops to campaign against the Arabs and Tibet, and asked for an imperial commission and the right to name his force.

sentences.zh: 玄宗甚嘉之，名軍為懷德軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzong greatly praised this and named the army the Huai De Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong warmly approved and named the force the Army of Cherishing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 九月，南天竺王尸利那羅僧伽寶多枝摩為國造寺，上表乞寺額，敕以歸化為名賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the king of South India Shilinaluosengge Baoduozimo built a temple for the state, submitted a memorial requesting a temple plaque, and an edict bestowed the name Guihua.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the South Indian king Shilinaluosengge Baoduozimo built a temple for his realm and petitioned for an imperial plaque; the throne granted the name "Return to Transformation."

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣使冊利那羅伽寶多為南天竺國王，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys were sent to invest Shilinaluoqiabao as king of South India, and envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month envoys invested Shilinaluoqiabao as king of South India, and a mission came to court.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，北天竺國（三）藏沙門僧密多獻質汗等藥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, the Tripitaka monk Simiduo of North India presented drugs such as zhizhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan (729), the Tripitaka monk Simiduo of North India presented medicinal preparations including zhizhan.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月，中天竺國王伊沙伏摩遣其大德僧來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year, the king of Central India Yishafumo sent his great virtuous monk to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan (731), King Yishafumo of Central India sent his chief monk to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十九年三月，中天竺王子李承恩來朝，授遊擊將軍，放還。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year, the prince of Central India Li Chengen came to court, was appointed General of Guerrilla Attacks, and was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Kaiyuan (741), Prince Li Chengen of Central India came to court, was made General of Guerrilla Attacks, and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，累遣使來。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, envoys were repeatedly sent.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tianbao era, missions arrived again and again.

sentences.zh: 罽賓國罽賓國，在蔥嶺南，去京師萬二千二百里。

translations.literal: Kapisa—Kapisa lies south of the Onion Mountains, twelve thousand two hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kapisa lay south of the Pamirs, twelve thousand two hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 常役屬於大月氏。

translations.literal: It was regularly subject to the Great Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was usually subject to the Great Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 其地暑濕，人皆乘象，土宜秔稻，草木淩寒不死。

translations.literal: The land was hot and damp; the people all rode elephants. The soil suited japonica rice; grasses and trees did not die even in severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was hot and humid, and people traveled by elephant. Japonica rice flourished there, and vegetation survived even bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 其俗尤信佛法。

translations.literal: Their custom especially honored the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: They were especially devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，引致西域，前後至者三十餘國，唯罽賓不至，

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Yang of Sui, the Western Regions were summoned; more than thirty states came in succession, but only Kapisa did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang of the Sui, the court drew in the Western Regions; more than thirty states came in turn, but Kapisa alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻名馬，太宗嘉其誠款，賜以繒彩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan, envoys were sent presenting famous horses. Taizong praised their sincere goodwill and bestowed silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan (637), envoys brought famed horses. Taizong commended their sincerity and rewarded them with silks.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又遣使獻褥特鼠，喙尖而尾赤，能食蛇，有被蛇螫者，鼠輒嗅而尿之，其瘡立愈，

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, envoys again presented the rute rat: its beak was sharp and its tail red; it could eat snakes. When someone was bitten by a snake, the rat would sniff the wound and urinate on it, and the sore would heal at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan (642), they sent the ichneumon—a sharp-beaked, red-tailed creature that ate snakes. If a man was snake-bitten, the animal would sniff the wound and urinate on it, and the injury healed immediately.

sentences.zh: 訪其國俗，云「王始祖馨孽，至今曷擷支，父子傳位，已十二代。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, they inquired into the customs of that country and were told: "The founding king was Xinnie; down to the present Hejiezhi, father and son have passed the throne through twelve generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing (658), envoys asked about local customs and learned: "The dynasty began with King Xinnie; down to the present Hejiezhi, twelve generations of fathers and sons have ruled in succession.

sentences.zh: 其年，改其城為修鮮都督府。

translations.literal: That same year its city was made the Xiuxian Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: That same year its capital was made the Xiuxian Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，授其王修鮮等十一州諸軍事兼修鮮都督，

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Longshuo era, its king was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the eleven prefectures including Xiuxian and concurrently Protector of Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longshuo era, its king was made commander-in-chief of eleven prefectures including Xiuxian and protector of Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 遣使來朝，進天文經一夾、秘要方並蕃藥等物，詔遣冊其王為葛羅達支特勒。

translations.literal: In the early Longshuo era, envoys came to court presenting a fascicle of astronomical texts, secret essential formulas, and foreign drugs; an edict invested their king as Geluodazhi Tele.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longshuo era, envoys came to court with astronomical texts, secret medical formulas, and foreign medicines; the throne invested their king as Geluodazhi Tele.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，其王烏散特勒灑以年老，上表請以子拂菻罽婆嗣位，許之，仍降使冊命，

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, its king Wusan Tele Sa, being old in years, submitted a memorial asking that his son Fulin Jipo succeed to the throne; this was granted, and envoys were still sent down to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan (739), King Wusan Tele Sa, grown old, asked that his son Fulin Jipo succeed him; the request was granted and investiture envoys were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 又冊其子勃匐準為襲罽賓及烏萇國王，仍授左驍衛將軍，

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan, his son Bofuzhun was also invested as successor king of Kapisa and Wuchang and was appointed General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That same year his son Bofuzhun was invested as heir to Kapisa and Wuchang and made General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 又遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan, envoys again came to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys again came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 勃律國又有勃律國，在罽賓、吐蕃之間。

translations.literal: Balur—there is also Balur, lying between Kapisa and Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Balur—another Balur—lay between Kapisa and Tibet.

sentences.zh: 開元中頻遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era envoys were frequently sent to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Kaiyuan era it sent frequent missions to court.

sentences.zh: 八年，冊立其王蘇麟陀逸之為勃律國王，朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, its king Sulintuoyizhi was invested as king of Balur, and tribute never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan (720), King Sulintuoyizhi was invested as ruler of Balur, and tribute continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為吐蕃所破。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, it was destroyed by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan (734), it was overrun by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 康國康國，即漢康居之國也。

translations.literal: Kang—Kang is the state of Han-times Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Kang—Kang was the Han-era kingdom of Kangju.

sentences.zh: 其王姓溫，月氏人也。

translations.literal: Its kings bore the surname Wen; they were Yuezhi people.
translations.idiomatic: Its kings were of the Wen clan and were Yuezhi by origin.

sentences.zh: 先居張掖祁連山北昭武城，為突厥所破，南依蔥嶺，遂有其地。

translations.literal: They first dwelt at Zhaowu city north of the Qilian Mountains in Zhangye; broken by the Turks, they moved south to rely on the Onion Mountains and then possessed this land.
translations.idiomatic: They had first lived at Zhaowu, north of the Qilian range in Zhangye; driven out by the Turks, they moved south to the Pamirs and took this territory.

sentences.zh: 枝庶皆以昭武為姓氏，不忘本也。

translations.literal: Branch and collateral lines all took Zhaowu as surname, not forgetting their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet branches all bore the surname Zhaowu, mindful of their origins.

sentences.zh: 其人皆深目高鼻，多須髯。

translations.literal: Its people all had deep-set eyes and high noses, with abundant beards.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes, high bridged noses, and heavy beards.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮或辮髮。

translations.literal: Men cut their hair short or wore it braided.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore their hair cropped or braided.

sentences.zh: 其王冠氈帽。

translations.literal: The king wore a felt cap.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a felt cap.

sentences.zh: 飾以金寶。

translations.literal: It was adorned with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: It was set with gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 婦人盤髻，幪以皁巾，飾以金花。

translations.literal: Women coiled their hair in a topknot, veiled it with a black cloth, and adorned it with golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore their hair in coils, covered with black cloth and ornamented with golden flowers.

sentences.zh: 人多嗜酒，好歌舞於道路。

translations.literal: The people greatly loved wine and delighted in song and dance along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: They loved wine and would sing and dance in the streets.

sentences.zh: 生子必以石蜜內口中，明膠置掌內，欲其成長口常甘言，掌持錢如膠之黏物。

translations.literal: When a child was born, rock honey was placed in its mouth and clarified glue in its palm, wishing that as it grew its mouth would always speak sweet words and its hand hold money as glue sticks to things.
translations.idiomatic: At birth, honey was placed in an infant's mouth and glue in its palm, so that it might grow up honey-tongued and tight-fisted.

sentences.zh: 俗習胡書。

translations.literal: Their custom used foreign script.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote in a foreign script.

sentences.zh: 善商賈，爭分銖之利。

translations.literal: They were skilled at trade and contended over fractions of cash.
translations.idiomatic: They were shrewd merchants who haggled over every coin.

sentences.zh: 男子年二十，即遠之旁國，來適中夏，利之所在，無所不到。

translations.literal: When a man reached twenty he was sent far to neighboring states; coming to the Central Plains, wherever profit lay, there was nowhere they would not go.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty a man was sent abroad; in the Central Plains they went wherever profit called.

sentences.zh: 以十二月為歲首，有婆羅門為之占星候氣，以定吉兇。

translations.literal: They took the twelfth month as the start of the year. Brahmins read the stars and observed the qi to determine fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The year began in the twelfth month. Brahmins read the stars and watched the winds to fix auspicious and inauspicious days.

sentences.zh: 頗有佛法。

translations.literal: There was considerable Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was widely practiced.

sentences.zh: 至十一月，鼓舞乞寒，以水相潑，盛為戲樂。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month they beat drums and begged off the cold, splashing one another with water in great festive sport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they held cold-weather festivals, beating drums and dousing one another with water in boisterous play.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，其王屈術支娶西突厥葉護可汗女，遂臣於西突厥，

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Yang of Sui, its king Qushuzhi married a daughter of the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan and then became subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang of the Sui, King Qushuzhi married a daughter of the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan and submitted to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 屈術支遣使獻名馬，

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wude, Qushuzhi sent envoys presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Wude (627), Qushuzhi sent envoys with famed horses.

sentences.zh: 又遣使貢獅子，太宗嘉其遠至，命秘書監虞世南為之賦，自此朝貢歲至。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, envoys again presented a lion. Taizong praised their coming from so far away and ordered Secretary Director Yu Shinan to compose a rhapsody for the occasion; from this tribute came every year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan (635), they sent a lion. Taizong praised their journey from so far and had Yu Shinan write a poem in its honor; thereafter tribute arrived yearly.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又獻金桃、銀桃，詔令植之於苑囿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, they again presented golden peaches and silver peaches; an edict ordered them planted in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan (723), they sent golden and silver peaches, and the throne ordered them planted in the palace gardens.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，則天封其大首領篤婆缽提為康國王，仍拜左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian year, Empress Wu invested the great chieftain Dubo Boti as king of Kang and also appointed him Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian reign, Empress Wu made the great chieftain Dubo Boti king of Kang and appointed him Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 缽提尋卒，又冊其子泥涅師師為康國王。

translations.literal: Boti soon died, and his son Ninie Shi was again invested as king of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Boti soon died, and his son Ninie Shi was invested as the next king of Kang.

sentences.zh: 師師以神龍中卒，國人又立突昏為王，

translations.literal: Shishi died in the Shenlong era, and the people again enthroned Tuhun as king.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi died during the Shenlong era, and the people raised Tuhun to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遣使貢獻鎖子甲、水精杯、馬腦瓶、駝鳥卵及越諾之類。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, envoys presented chain-mail armor, crystal cups, agate bottles, ostrich eggs, and goods such as yuenuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan (718), envoys brought chain mail, crystal cups, agate flasks, ostrich eggs, and other rarities.

sentences.zh: 十九年，其王烏勒上表，請封其子咄曷為曹國王，默啜為米國王，許之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, its king Wule submitted a memorial requesting that his sons Zhuohe be invested as king of Cao and Mochuo as king of Mi; this was granted.
