translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan (731), King Wule asked that his sons Zhuohe and Mochuo be made kings of Cao and Mi; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，烏勒卒，遣使冊咄曷襲父位，

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Wule died and envoys were sent to invest Zhuohe as successor to his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan (739), Wule died and envoys invested Zhuohe as his successor.

sentences.zh: 又封為欽化王，其母可敦封為郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he was again invested as Prince of Qinhua, and his mother the Khatun was invested as Lady of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao (744), he was further invested as Prince of Qinhua, and his mother the khatun was made Lady of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一載、十三載，並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and thirteenth years, envoys were both sent to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh and thirteenth years of Tianbao, missions came to court.

sentences.zh: 波斯國波斯國，在京師西一萬五千三百里，東與吐火羅、康國接，北鄰突厥之可薩部，西北拒拂菻，正西及南俱臨大海。

translations.literal: Persia—Persia lies fifteen thousand three hundred li west of the capital. To the east it borders Tuhuoluo and Kang; to the north it neighbors the Qasar division of the Turks; to the northwest it faces Fulin; due west and south it all fronts the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: Persia lay fifteen thousand three hundred li west of the capital, bordering Tuhuoluo and Kang on the east, the Qasar Turks on the north, and Fulin to the northwest, with the open sea to west and south.

sentences.zh: 戶數十萬。

translations.literal: Households numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Its population ran to several hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其王居有二城，復有大城十餘，猶中國之離宮。

translations.literal: Its king dwelt in two cities, and there were also more than ten great cities—like detached palaces in China.
translations.idiomatic: The king maintained two capitals and more than ten great cities besides, like the detached palaces of China.

sentences.zh: 其王初嗣位，便密選子才堪承統者，書其名字，封而藏之。

translations.literal: When the king first succeeded to the throne, he secretly selected whichever son was capable of inheriting the succession, wrote his name, sealed and hid it.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne, the king secretly chose whichever son could rule, wrote down his name, sealed the record, and hid it away.

sentences.zh: 王死後，大臣與王之群子共發封而視之，奉所書名者為主焉。

translations.literal: After the king died, the great ministers together with all the king's sons opened the seal and looked; they installed as ruler the one whose name was written.
translations.idiomatic: When the king died, the ministers and all the princes opened the seal together and enthroned the name written within.

sentences.zh: 其王冠金花冠，坐獅子床，服錦袍，加以瓔珞。

translations.literal: The king wore a golden-flower crown, sat on a lion couch, wore a brocade robe, and was further adorned with a jeweled collar.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a crown of golden flowers, sat upon a lion throne, dressed in brocade, and wore a collar of jewels.

sentences.zh: 俗事天地日月水火之諸神，西域諸胡事火祅者，皆詣波斯受法焉。

translations.literal: By custom they worship the various gods of heaven, earth, sun, moon, water, and fire; all the Western Region Hu who tend the sacred fire come to Persia to receive the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The people worship heaven, earth, sun, moon, water, and fire. Every fire-worshiping Hu people of the Western Regions journeyed to Persia to receive the law.

sentences.zh: 其事神，以麝香和蘇塗須點額，及於耳鼻，用以為敬，拜必交股。

translations.literal: In serving the gods they mix musk with sappanwood, paint the beard, mark the forehead and also the ears and nose—this is their reverence; in bowing they must cross the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: In worship they mixed musk with sappanwood, painted their beards, and marked forehead, ears, and nose as signs of reverence. When they bowed, they crossed their thighs.

sentences.zh: 文字同於諸胡。

translations.literal: Their script is the same as the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing matched that of the other Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 男女皆徒跣。

translations.literal: Men and women alike go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮，戴白皮帽，衣不開襟，並有巾帔，多用蘇方青白色為之，兩邊緣以織成錦。

translations.literal: Husbands cut their hair, wear white leather caps, and garments that do not open at the front; they all have turbans and mantles, mostly made in sappanwood blue and white, with woven brocade edging both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair, wore white leather caps, and closed-front robes with turbans and mantles—usually dyed sappanwood blue or white, the hems edged in woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 婦人亦巾帔裙衫，辮髮垂後，飾以金銀，其國乘象而戰，每一象，戰士百人，有敗恤者則盡殺之。

translations.literal: Women also wear turbans, mantles, skirts, and jackets; they braid their hair to hang behind and adorn themselves with gold and silver. The state fights mounted on elephants; for each elephant there are a hundred warriors, and those defeated in battle are all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore turbans, mantles, skirts, and jackets, their braided hair hanging down their backs and trimmed with gold and silver. The army fought from elephant back—one hundred soldiers to each beast—and any company defeated was put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 國人生女，年十歲已上有姿貌者，其王收而養之，以賞有功之臣。

translations.literal: When the people bear a daughter of fine appearance from age ten upward, the king takes and raises her to reward ministers who have merit.
translations.idiomatic: When a subject's daughter of ten or more showed exceptional beauty, the king took her into the palace and later bestowed her on ministers who had earned merit.

sentences.zh: 俗右尊而左卑。

translations.literal: By custom the right is honored and the left is low.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the right ranked above the left.

sentences.zh: 以六月一日為歲首。

translations.literal: They take the first day of the sixth month as the start of the year.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned the year from the first day of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 斷獄不為文書約束，口決於庭。

translations.literal: In deciding cases they are not bound by written documents; judgment is spoken in court.
translations.idiomatic: Trials were decided without written codes—judgment was pronounced aloud in open court.

sentences.zh: 其系囚無年限，唯王者代立則釋之。

translations.literal: Those imprisoned have no fixed term; only when a new king succeeds are they released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were held without fixed terms and were released only when a new king took the throne.

sentences.zh: 其叛逆之罪，就火祅燒鐵灼其舌，瘡白者為理直，瘡黑者為有罪。

translations.literal: For the crime of rebellion, at the fire altar they heat iron and cauterize the tongue; if the sore turns white the case is just, if black the person is guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were tried at the fire altar: iron was heated and the tongue cauterized. A white scar meant innocence; a black scar meant guilt.

sentences.zh: 其刑有斷手、刖足、髡鉗、劓刖，輕罪翦鬚，或繋牌於項以誌之，經時月而釋焉。

translations.literal: Their punishments include severing hands, cutting off feet, shaving the head and clamping, cutting nose and feet; for light crimes they cut the beard, or tie a placard on the neck as a mark—after months and seasons they are released.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments ranged from severed hands and feet to shaved heads in irons and mutilation of nose or legs. Minor offenses brought a clipped beard or a placard tied at the neck; after a season or two the mark was removed.

sentences.zh: 其強盜一入獄，至老更不出，小盜罰以銀錢。

translations.literal: Armed robbers, once imprisoned, never leave even in old age; petty thieves are fined in silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: Armed robbers entered prison for life; petty thieves paid fines in silver.

sentences.zh: 死亡則棄之於山，制服一月而即吉。

translations.literal: When someone dies they abandon the body on a mountain; after one month in mourning garb they then observe auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were left on the mountains. Mourning dress was worn for a month, then life resumed.

sentences.zh: 氣候暑熱，土地寬平，知耕種，多畜牧，有鳥形如橐駝，飛不能高，食草及肉，亦能噉犬攫羊，土人極以為患。

translations.literal: The climate is hot; the land broad and level. They know tilling and sowing and keep much livestock. There is a bird shaped like a camel, unable to fly high; it eats grass and meat and can even devour dogs and seize goats—the natives find it a grave pest.
translations.idiomatic: The climate ran hot and the land lay broad and flat. The people farmed and kept large herds. A bird shaped like a camel, too heavy to fly high, ate grass and flesh alike and even attacked dogs and snatched goats—the natives counted it a terrible scourge.

sentences.zh: 又多白馬、駿犬，或赤日行七百里者駮，金犬今所謂波斯犬也。

translations.literal: They also have many white horses and swift hounds; some piebald ones can run seven hundred li in a single day. The golden hound is what is now called the Persian hound.
translations.idiomatic: White horses and swift hounds abounded; some piebald dogs could run seven hundred li in a day. The golden hound was what people now call the Persian dog.

sentences.zh: 出䮫及大驢、師子、白象、珊瑚樹高一二尺，琥珀、車渠、瑪瑙、火珠、玻璃、琉璃、無食子、香附子、訶黎勒、胡椒、蓽撥、石蜜、千年棗、甘露桃。

translations.literal: They export mules and great donkeys, lions, white elephants, coral trees one or two chi high, amber, carnelian, agate, fire pearls, crystal, lapis lazuli, myrobalan, cyperus, harītakī, pepper, long pepper, rock honey, millennial jujubes, and honey peaches.
translations.idiomatic: They exported mules and great donkeys, lions, white elephants, coral trees a foot or two tall, amber, carnelian, agate, fire pearls, crystal, lapis lazuli, myrobalan, cyperus root, harītakī, pepper, long pepper, rock honey, thousand-year jujubes, and honey peaches.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，西突厥葉護可汗頻擊破其國，波斯王庫薩和為西突厥所殺，其子施利立，葉護因分其部帥，監統其國，波斯竟臣於葉護。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye of Sui, the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan repeatedly smashed their state. The Persian king Khusraw was killed by the Western Turks; his son Shiluoli succeeded. The Yabghu divided his tribal chiefs to oversee and rule the country, and Persia ultimately became subject to the Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign, the Western Turk Yabghu Qaghan repeatedly broke Persia. King Khusraw was slain by the Western Turks, and his son Shiluoli took the throne. The Yabghu posted his tribal chiefs to oversee the realm, and Persia at last submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 及葉護可汗死，其所令監統者因自擅於波斯，不復役屬於西突厥。

translations.literal: When the Yabghu Qaghan died, those he had set to oversee took sole control in Persia and no longer served the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yabghu died, the overseers he had appointed seized power in Persia and ceased to answer to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 施利立一年卒，乃立庫薩和之女為王，突厥又殺之。

translations.literal: Shiluoli died after one year on the throne; Khusraw's daughter was then raised as queen, and the Turks killed her too.
translations.idiomatic: Shiluoli reigned one year and died. Khusraw's daughter was then enthroned, and the Turks killed her as well.

sentences.zh: 施利之子單羯方奔拂菻，於是國人迎而立之，是為尹恆支，在位二年而卒。

translations.literal: Shiluoli's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin; the people thereupon welcomed and established him—this was Yin Hengzhi, who reigned two years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shiluoli's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin. The Persians welcomed him home and made him king—Yin Hengzhi, who ruled two years and died.

sentences.zh: 兄子伊嗣候立。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Yazdegerd succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yazdegerd succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，伊嗣候遣使獻一獸，名活褥蛇，形類鼠而色青，身長八九寸，能入穴取鼠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Yazdegerd sent envoys presenting a beast called the huoruo snake, ratlike in form and blue in color, eight or nine cun long, able to enter holes and catch rats.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan (733), Yazdegerd sent envoys with a creature called the huoruo snake—rat-shaped, blue-green, eight or nine inches long, and able to enter burrows and seize rats.

sentences.zh: 伊嗣候懦弱，為大首領所逐，遂奔吐火羅，未至，亦為大食兵所殺。

translations.literal: Yazdegerd was weak; pursued by a great chieftain, he fled toward Tuhuoluo but was killed by Arab troops before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yazdegerd proved timid. A great chieftain drove him out; he fled toward Tuhuoluo but was cut down by Arab soldiers before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 其子名卑路斯，又投吐火羅葉護，獲免。

translations.literal: His son, named Peroz, then sought refuge with the Tuhuoluo yabghu and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His son Peroz took refuge with the Tuhuoluo yabghu and was spared.

sentences.zh: 卑路斯奏言頻被大食侵擾，請兵救援。

translations.literal: Peroz memorialized that he was repeatedly harassed by Arab invasions and requested troops for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Peroz petitioned that Arab raids were unceasing and begged for troops to save him.

sentences.zh: 詔遣隴州南由縣令王名遠充使西域，分置州縣，因列其地疾陵城為波斯都督府，授卑路斯為都督。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Wang Mingyuan, magistrate of Nanyou in Long Prefecture, as envoy to the Western Regions to divide and establish prefectures and counties; accordingly Jiling city in that land was listed as the Persian Protectorate, and Peroz was appointed protector.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Wang Mingyuan, magistrate of Nanyou in Long Prefecture, as envoy to the west to parcel out prefectures and counties. Jiling was made seat of the Persian Protectorate, and Peroz was named protector.

sentences.zh: 是後數遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: After this envoys were repeatedly sent bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter missions came again and again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，卑路斯自來入朝，高宗甚加恩賜，拜右武衛將軍，

translations.literal: During Xianheng, Peroz came in person to court; Gaozong greatly favored him and appointed him Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng era, Peroz came to court in person. Emperor Gaozong heaped favors on him and made him Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 令吏部侍郎裴行儉將兵冊送卑路斯為波斯王，行儉以其路遠，至安西碎葉而還，卑路斯獨返，不得入其國，漸為大食所侵，客於吐火羅國二十餘年，有部落數千人，後漸離散。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Pei Xingjian was ordered to lead troops to invest and escort Peroz as king of Persia. Xingjian, finding the road too far, reached Suyab in Anxi and returned; Peroz returned alone, unable to enter his country, and was gradually invaded by the Arabs. He sojourned in Tuhuoluo more than twenty years with a tribe of several thousand before they gradually scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng (678), Vice Minister Pei Xingjian was ordered to escort Peroz home as king of Persia. Finding the route too long, Xingjian turned back at Suyab in Anxi. Peroz went on alone but could not re-enter his realm and was slowly ground down by the Arabs. He lived as a guest in Tuhuoluo for more than twenty years with a following of several thousand before it dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 至，又來入朝，拜為左威衛將軍，無何病卒，其國遂滅，而部眾猶存。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong he again came to court and was appointed General of the Left Majestic Guard; before long he died of illness. The state was extinguished, but bands of followers remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong (708) he returned to court and was made General of the Left Majestic Guard. He soon died of illness. The kingdom was gone, but scattered bands of his people survived.

sentences.zh: 自至，凡十遣使來朝，並獻方物。

translations.literal: From the tenth year of Kaiyuan to the sixth year of Tianbao, ten missions came to court in all, each bringing local products.
translations.idiomatic: From the tenth year of Kaiyuan to the sixth year of Tianbao (722–747), ten embassies came to court bearing regional goods.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣使獻瑪瑙床。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, envoys presented an agate couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, envoys presented an agate couch.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，獻火毛繡舞筵、長毛繡舞筵、無孔真珠，

translations.literal: In the ninth year, fourth month, they presented fire-wool embroidered dance mats, long-wool embroidered dance mats, and flawless pearls.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan (721), in the fourth month, they brought fire-wool embroidered dance mats, long-wool embroidered dance mats, and pearls without bore.

sentences.zh: 波斯與大食同寇廣州，劫倉庫，焚廬舍，浮海而去，

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, Persia and the Arabs together raided Guangzhou, plundered the storehouses, burned the buildings, and put to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan (758), Persians and Arabs together raided Guangzhou, looted the warehouses, burned the quarters, and sailed away.

sentences.zh: 遣使來朝，獻真珠等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dali, envoys came to court and presented pearls and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dali (771), envoys came to court with pearls and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 拂菻國拂菻國，一名大秦，在西海之上，東南與波斯接，地方萬餘里，列城四百，邑居連屬。

translations.literal: Fulin—Fulin, also called Daqin, lies above the Western Sea. Southeast it borders Persia; its territory exceeds ten thousand li, with four hundred walled cities and settlements linked in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fulin—also called Daqin—lay beyond the Western Sea, bordering Persia to the southeast. Its domain ran more than ten thousand li, with four hundred cities and towns strung together.

sentences.zh: 其宮宇柱櫳，多以水精琉璃為之。

translations.literal: Its palaces and halls have pillars and balustrades mostly made of crystal and glass.
translations.idiomatic: Palace pillars and balustrades were mostly crystal and glass.

sentences.zh: 有貴臣十二人共治國政，常使一人將囊隨王車，百姓有事者，即以書投囊中，王還宮省發，理其枉直。

translations.literal: Twelve great ministers jointly govern state affairs; one is always made to carry a bag beside the royal carriage. When common people have business, they put a written petition in the bag; when the king returns to the palace he opens and reads them, settling right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve senior ministers governed together. One always rode beside the king with a satchel at his belt; subjects slipped petitions inside, and when the king returned to the palace he read them and judged each case.

sentences.zh: 其王無常人，簡賢者而立之。

translations.literal: Their king is not a fixed person; they select the worthy and establish him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was not hereditary—the worthiest man was chosen to rule.

sentences.zh: 國中災異及風雨不時，輒廢而更立。

translations.literal: When calamities or untimely wind and rain occur in the state, they depose the ruler and install another.
translations.idiomatic: If omens or ill-timed storms troubled the realm, the king was deposed and another raised.

sentences.zh: 其王冠形如鳥舉翼，冠及瓔珞，皆綴以珠寶，著錦繡衣，前不開襟，坐金花床。

translations.literal: The king's crown is shaped like a bird spreading its wings; crown and collar are all strung with jewels. He wears brocade garments closed at the front and sits on a golden-flower couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a crown shaped like a bird with wings spread, crown and collar studded with gems. He dressed in brocade closed at the front and sat on a golden-flower throne.

sentences.zh: 有一鳥似鵝，其毛綠色，常在王邊倚枕上坐，每進食有毒，其鳥輒鳴。

translations.literal: There is a bird like a goose, green in plumage, that always sits beside the king on his pillow-rest. Whenever poison is in food presented, the bird cries out.
translations.idiomatic: A goose-like bird with green feathers perched by the king's pillow. If food was poisoned, the bird shrieked.

sentences.zh: 其都城疊石為之，尤絕高峻，凡有十萬餘戶，南臨大海。

translations.literal: The capital is built of piled stone, exceedingly high and steep, with more than one hundred thousand households; south it fronts the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was built of stacked stone, towering and sheer, holding more than one hundred thousand households and facing the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 城東面有大門，其高二十餘丈，自上及下，飾以黃金，光輝燦爛，連曜數里。

translations.literal: On the east of the city is a great gate more than twenty zhang high; from top to bottom it is adorned with gold, shining brilliantly for several li.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city stood a gate more than twenty zhang tall, gilded from summit to base so that its radiance ran for several li.

sentences.zh: 自外至王室，凡有大門三重，列異寶雕飾。

translations.literal: From the outer precincts to the royal residence there are three great gates in all, arrayed with rare treasures and carved ornament.
translations.idiomatic: From the outer walls to the royal residence ran three great gates, each set with rare treasures and carved ornament.

sentences.zh: 第二門之樓中，懸一大金秤，以金丸十二枚屬於衡端，以候日之十二時焉；

translations.literal: In the tower of the second gate hangs a great golden scale, with twelve golden balls attached to the beam end to mark the twelve hours of the day;
translations.idiomatic: In the tower of the second gate hung a great golden balance with twelve golden balls on the beam to mark the twelve hours of the day;

sentences.zh: 為一金人，其大如人，立於側，每至一時，其金丸輒落，鏗然發聲，引唱以紀日時，毫厘無失。

translations.literal: a golden figure as large as a man stands at the side; at each hour a ball drops with a ringing sound, and a voice calls out to record the time—not a hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: beside it stood a golden figure life-size. At each hour a ball fell with a clang and a voice called the time—never off by a hair.

sentences.zh: 其殿以瑟瑟為柱，黃金為地，象牙為門扇，香木為棟梁。

translations.literal: The hall has sese stone for pillars, gold for flooring, ivory for door panels, and fragrant wood for beams.
translations.idiomatic: The hall had sese-stone pillars, gold flooring, ivory doors, and fragrant-wood beams.

sentences.zh: 其俗無瓦，搗白石為末，羅之塗屋上，其堅密光潤，還如玉石。

translations.literal: By custom they have no tiles; they pound white stone to powder, sift it, and spread it on roofs—the result is hard, close, and lustrous like jade stone.
translations.idiomatic: They used no roof tiles. White stone was pounded to dust, sifted, and spread on the roofs until the surface hardened bright as jade.

sentences.zh: 至於盛暑之節，人厭囂熱，乃引水潛流，上遍於屋宇，機制巧密，人莫之知。

translations.literal: In the height of summer, when people loathe the heat and clamor, they lead water in hidden channels flowing over the rooftops—the mechanism is ingeniously concealed and none know how it works.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer, when the heat grew unbearable, water was run in hidden channels across the rooftops—the mechanism so cunning that none could see how it worked.

sentences.zh: 觀者惟聞屋上泉鳴，俄見四檐飛溜，懸波如瀑，激氣成涼風，其巧妙如此。

translations.literal: Spectators hear only the spring murmur on the roofs; suddenly the four eaves pour flying streams, suspended waves like waterfalls, and the rushing air becomes a cool breeze—so artful is the device.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners heard only springs murmuring over the roofs; then all at once water sheeted from the four eaves like hanging waterfalls, and the rush of air turned to a cool wind—such was its artifice.

sentences.zh: 風俗，男子翦髮，披帔而右袒，婦人不開襟，錦為頭巾。

translations.literal: Customs: men cut their hair, drape mantles and bare the right shoulder; women do not open their garments at the front and use brocade for headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: In dress, men cropped their hair, wore mantles draped over the right shoulder, and women kept closed-front robes with brocade headcloths.

sentences.zh: 家資滿億，封以上位。

translations.literal: Households with wealth reaching a hundred million are ennobled to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Any household whose wealth reached a hundred million was ennobled to high rank.

sentences.zh: 有羊羔生於土中，其國人候其欲萌，乃築墻以院之，防外獸所食也。

translations.literal: There are lambs born from the earth; when the people see them about to sprout, they build walls to enclose them, lest outside beasts eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Lambs were said to sprout from the soil. When a shoot appeared, the people walled it in to keep wild beasts away.

sentences.zh: 然其臍與地連，割之則死，唯人著甲走馬及擊鼓以駭之，其羔警鳴而臍絕，便遂水草。

translations.literal: Yet its navel is joined to the ground—cut it and the lamb dies. Only if men in armor run horses and beat drums to frighten it will the lamb cry out, the navel sever, and it then seek grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: Its navel remained rooted to the earth; cut it and the lamb died. Men in armor had to gallop horses and beat drums to startle it—only when the lamb cried out would the cord break and it run free to graze.

sentences.zh: 俗皆髡而衣繡，乘輜軿白蓋小車，出入擊鼓，建旌旗幡幟。

translations.literal: By custom all shave the head and wear embroidered dress; they ride covered carriages with white canopies, beating drums when going out and raising banners and pennants.
translations.idiomatic: All shaved their heads and wore embroidered robes. They rode in covered carriages with white canopies, beating drums when they went abroad and flying banners and pennants.

sentences.zh: 土多金銀奇寶，有夜光璧、明月珠、駭雞犀、大貝、車渠、瑪瑙、孔翠、珊瑚、琥珀，凡西域諸珍異多出其國。

translations.literal: The soil yields much gold, silver, and rare treasures: luminous jade disks, moon-pearls, cock-frightening rhinoceros horn, great shells, carnelian, agate, kingfisher feathers, coral, amber—most of the Western Regions' marvels come from this country.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and rare treasures filled the land—night-shining disks, moon pearls, cock-frightening rhinoceros horn, great shells, carnelian, agate, kingfisher plumes, coral, amber. Most of the west's wonders came from there.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝常將通拂菻，竟不能致，

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui often intended to open relations with Fulin but never succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of the Sui often sought contact with Fulin but never achieved it.

sentences.zh: 拂菻王波多力遣使獻赤玻璃、綠金精等物，太宗降璽書答慰，賜以綾綺焉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, King Boduoli of Fulin sent envoys presenting red glass, green gold essence, and other objects; Taizong returned an imperial letter of consolation and bestowed silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan (643), King Boduoli of Fulin sent envoys with red glass, green gold essence, and other gifts. Emperor Taizong answered with an imperial letter of thanks and gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 自大食強盛，漸陵諸國，乃遣大將軍摩栧伐其都城，因約為和好，請每歲輸之金帛，遂臣屬大食焉，

translations.literal: As the Arabs grew strong and gradually dominated the various states, they sent the great general Muhan to attack its capital, then made a pact of peace and demanded yearly tribute of gold and silk, whereupon Fulin became subject to the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: When Arab power rose and overawed the western kingdoms, they sent the general Muhan against the Fulin capital, then made peace on condition of yearly gold and silk. Fulin became an Arab vassal.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻底也伽，

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng, envoys presented a diye jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfeng (667), envoys presented a diye jia.

sentences.zh: 復遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, envoys again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazu (701), envoys again came to court.

sentences.zh: 正月，其主遣吐火羅大首領獻獅子、羚羊各二。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Kaiyuan, its ruler sent a great chieftain of Tuhuoluo presenting two lions and two antelopes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of Kaiyuan (719), its ruler sent a Tuhuoluo chieftain with two lions and two antelopes.

sentences.zh: 不數月，又遣大德僧來朝貢。

translations.literal: Within a few months they again sent a great virtue monk to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Within months a senior monk came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 大食國大食國，本在波斯之西。

translations.literal: The Arab state— the Arab state originally lay west of Persia.
translations.idiomatic: The Arab realm—the Arab realm originally lay west of Persia.

sentences.zh: 大業中，有波斯胡人牧駝於俱紛摩地那之山，忽有獅子人語謂之曰：「此山西有三穴，穴中大有兵器，汝可取之。

translations.literal: During Daye, a Persian Hu herding camels on Mount Jufenmo Dina suddenly heard a lion speak to him, saying: "West of this mountain are three caves; inside are many weapons—you may take them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, a Persian camel-herder on Mount Jufenmo Dina heard a lion speak: "West of this mountain are three caves full of weapons. Take them.

sentences.zh: 穴中並有黑石白文，讀之便作王位。」

translations.literal: In the caves are also black stones with white writing; read them and you will become king."
translations.idiomatic: Inside are black stones marked with white script. Read them and you shall be king."

sentences.zh: 胡人依言，果見穴中有石及槊刃甚多，上有文，教其反叛。

translations.literal: The Hu followed the words and indeed saw in the caves many stones and spear-blades; on them was writing instructing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The man obeyed and found stones and blades in plenty, inscribed with words urging revolt.

sentences.zh: 於是糾合亡命，渡恆曷水，劫奪商旅，其眾漸盛，遂割據波斯西境，自立為王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered desperadoes, crossed the Hengge River, plundered merchants, and as his force grew he carved out the western marches of Persia and declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied outlaws, crossed the Hengge River, and preyed on caravans until his band swelled. He seized Persia's western marches and crowned himself king.

sentences.zh: 波斯、拂菻各遣兵討之，皆為所敗，

translations.literal: Persia and Fulin each sent troops to punish him, but both were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Persia and Fulin sent armies against him and were both beaten.

sentences.zh: 始遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, they first sent envoys to pay tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui (651), they first sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其王姓大食氏，名噉密莫末膩，自云有國已三十四年，歷三主矣。

translations.literal: Their king's surname is Dashi; his name Tanmi Momoni; he says the state has existed thirty-four years and three rulers have passed.
translations.idiomatic: The king's clan was Dashi; his name Tanmi Momoni. He said his realm had stood thirty-four years under three rulers.

sentences.zh: 其國男兒色黑多鬚，鼻大而長，似婆羅門；

translations.literal: The men of the country are dark-skinned and bearded, with large long noses, resembling Brahmins;
translations.idiomatic: Its men were dark and bearded, with large long noses like Brahmins;

sentences.zh: 婦人白皙。

translations.literal: the women are fair-skinned.
translations.idiomatic: its women fair-skinned.

sentences.zh: 亦有文字。

translations.literal: They also have a written script.
translations.idiomatic: They had a written script as well.

sentences.zh: 出駝馬，大於諸國。

translations.literal: They produce camels and horses larger than other countries.
translations.idiomatic: Their camels and horses outstripped those of other lands.

sentences.zh: 兵刃勁利。

translations.literal: Their weapons are keen.
translations.idiomatic: Their blades were sharp.

sentences.zh: 其俗勇於戰鬥，好事天神。

translations.literal: By custom they are bold in battle and devoted to the heavenly god.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce in war and devoted to the heavenly god.

sentences.zh: 土多沙石，不堪耕種，唯食駝馬等肉。

translations.literal: The soil is mostly sand and stone, unsuited to farming; they eat only camel, horse, and other meat.
translations.idiomatic: Sand and rock covered the ground, good for neither plow nor seed—they lived on camel, horse, and other flesh.

sentences.zh: 俱紛摩地那山在國之西南，鄰於大海，其王移穴中黑石置之於國。

translations.literal: Mount Jufenmo Dina is in the southwest of the country, bordering the great sea; the king moved the black stone from the cave and set it in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jufenmo Dina stood in the country's southwest by the sea. The king brought the black stone from the cave and enshrined it in his realm.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遣人乘船，將衣糧入海，經八年而未及西岸。

translations.literal: They also once sent men in ships with clothing and grain out to sea; after eight years they had not yet reached the western shore.
translations.idiomatic: Once they sent men to sea in ships stocked with food and clothing; eight years passed and they still had not sighted the western shore.

sentences.zh: 海中見一方石，石上有樹，幹赤葉青，樹上總生小兒；

translations.literal: At sea they saw a square stone; on the stone was a tree, red trunk and green leaves, and on the tree grew many small children;
translations.idiomatic: At sea they came upon a square stone bearing a tree with a red trunk and green leaves, and on its branches hung many small children;

sentences.zh: 長六七寸，見人皆笑，動其手腳，頭著樹枝，其使摘取一枝，小兒便死，收在大食王宮。

translations.literal: six or seven cun tall, they all laughed when they saw people, moving hands and feet; their heads were attached to the branches. The envoy plucked one branch and the child died; it was kept in the Arab king's palace.
translations.idiomatic: each six or seven inches tall, laughing and waving at passersby, heads fixed to the boughs. An envoy broke off a branch; the child died at once. The king kept it in his palace.

sentences.zh: 又有女國，在其西北，相去三月行。

translations.literal: There is also a women's country northwest of them, three months' journey away.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay a women's kingdom three months' travel distant.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，擊破波斯，又破拂菻，始有米麪之屬。

translations.literal: At the start of Longshuo they broke Persia and also broke Fulin, and then had rice and flour and the like.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longshuo era they crushed Persia and Fulin alike and came to possess grain and flour.

sentences.zh: 又將兵南侵婆羅門，吞並諸胡國，勝兵四十餘萬。

translations.literal: They again led troops south to invade Brahman lands, swallowing the various Hu states; their effective troops exceeded four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They marched south against Brahman lands and swallowed the Hu kingdoms until their field army passed four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 長安中，遣使獻良馬，

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, envoys presented fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, envoys brought fine horses.

sentences.zh: 又獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, they again presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun (711), they again presented local products.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遣使來朝，進馬及寶鈿帶等方物。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaiyuan, envoys came to court, advancing horses and jeweled girdles and other local products.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaiyuan, envoys came with horses, jeweled girdles, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 其使謁見，唯平立不拜，憲司欲糾之，中書令張說奏曰：「大食殊俗，慕義遠來，不可置罪。」

translations.literal: When their envoy had audience he merely stood erect and did not bow; the censorate wished to indict him. Chief Minister Zhang Yue memorialized: "The Arabs are a wholly different custom, come from afar in admiration of righteousness—we cannot punish them."
translations.idiomatic: At audience their envoy stood straight and did not bow. The censorate moved to indict him, but Chief Minister Zhang Yue argued: "The Arabs are a foreign people who have come far in admiration of our virtue. We cannot punish them."

sentences.zh: 上特許之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the exception.

sentences.zh: 尋又遣使朝獻，自云在本國惟拜天神，雖見王亦無致拜之法，所司屢詰責之，其使遂請依漢法致拜。

translations.literal: Soon they again sent envoys to court; they said that in their own land they worship only the heavenly god and even on seeing a king have no method of bowing—the responsible offices repeatedly rebuked them, whereupon the envoys asked to bow according to Han law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another embassy arrived. They explained that at home they worshipped only the heavenly god and even before their own king knew no bow—officials rebuked them again and again until the envoys asked to bow by Han rite.

sentences.zh: 其時西域康國、石國之類，皆臣屬之。

translations.literal: At that time Kang, Shi, and the like in the Western Regions were all subject to them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Kang, Shi, and the other Western Region states all bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 其境東西萬里，東與突騎施相接焉。

translations.literal: Their territory east and west is ten thousand li; east it meets the Turgesh.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran ten thousand li east to west, meeting the Turgesh on the east.

sentences.zh: 一云隋開皇中，大食族中有孤列種代為酋長，孤列種中又有兩姓：一號盆泥奚深，一號盆泥末換。

translations.literal: One account says that in Kaihuang of Sui among the Arab tribes there was the Gulie clan serving as chieftains in succession; within the Gulie there were two surnames: one called Peni Xishen, one called Peni Mohuan.
translations.idiomatic: One version says that in the Kaihuang era of Sui, among the Arab tribes the Gulie clan held the chieftainship in turn; within Gulie were two lines, Peni Xishen and Peni Mohuan.

sentences.zh: 其奚深後有摩訶末者，勇健多智，眾立之為主，東西征伐，開地三千里，兼克夏臘，一名釤城。

translations.literal: After Xishen there was Mohemo, brave, strong, and wise; the multitude established him as lord. He campaigned east and west, opening territory three thousand li, and also conquered Xiala, also called Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xishen line came Mohemo, bold and clever, whom the people made lord. He conquered east and west until his realm stretched three thousand li, taking Xiala—also called Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 摩訶末後十四代，至末換。

translations.literal: Fourteen generations after Mohemo came Mohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen generations after Mohemo came Mohuan.

sentences.zh: 末換殺其兄伊疾而自立，復殘忍，其下怨之。

translations.literal: Mohuan killed his elder brother Yiji and established himself; again cruel, his subordinates resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuan murdered his elder brother Yiji and seized the throne. His cruelty bred resentment among his followers.

sentences.zh: 有呼羅珊木粗人並波悉林舉義兵，應者悉令著黑衣，旬月間眾盈數萬。

translations.literal: There were men of Khurasan, Mucu, and Bosilin who raised righteous troops; all who answered were ordered to wear black garments, and within a month or so their masses exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Khurasan, Mucu, and Bosilin raised rebel armies; every follower was ordered to wear black, and within a month their numbers swelled past ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鼓行而西，生擒末換，殺之。

translations.literal: Beating drums they marched west, captured Muhuan alive, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They marched west with drums beating, took Muhuan alive, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 遂求得奚深種阿蒲羅拔，立之。

translations.literal: They thereupon sought out the Xishen clan's Abu Luobo and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: They then found Abu Luobo of the Xishen clan and set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 末換已前謂之「白衣大食」，自阿蒲羅拔後改為「黑衣大食」。

translations.literal: Before Muhuan they were called the "White-Clad Arabs"; from Abu Luobo onward they were changed to the "Black-Clad Arabs."
translations.idiomatic: Before Muhuan they were known as the White-Clad Arabs; after Abu Luobo they became the Black-Clad Arabs.

sentences.zh: 阿蒲羅拔卒，立其弟阿蒲恭拂。

translations.literal: When Abu Luobo died, his younger brother Abu Gongfu was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: When Abu Luobo died, his brother Abu Gongfu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 至德初遣使朝貢，代宗時為元帥，亦用其國兵以收兩都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he sent envoys to court with tribute; during Daizong's time he served as commander-in-chief and likewise used his state's troops to recover the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era he sent tribute envoys; under Daizong he served as commander-in-chief and contributed his troops to the recovery of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 寶應、大曆中頻遣使來。

translations.literal: During Baoying and Dali he frequently sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying and Dali eras he sent envoys repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 恭拂卒，子迷地立。

translations.literal: When Gongfu died, his son Midi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongfu died, his son Midi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 迷地卒，子牟棲立，牟棲卒，弟訶論立。

translations.literal: When Midi died, his son Muqi succeeded; when Muqi died, his younger brother Helun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was succeeded by his son Muqi; when Muqi died, his brother Helun took the throne.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，與吐蕃為勍敵。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era they were fierce enemies of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era they were formidable rivals of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 蕃軍太半西禦大食，故鮮為邊患，其力不足也。

translations.literal: Most of the Tibetan army faced west to resist the Arabs, so they rarely became a border menace—their strength was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Most Tibetan forces were tied up in the west against the Arabs, so they seldom threatened the frontier; their power was simply not enough.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔以黑衣大食使含嵯、焉雞、沙北三人並為中郎將，各放還蕃。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict appointed the Black-Clad Arab envoys Hanzuo, Yanji, and Shabei all as Gentlemen of the Palace, and each was released to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Black Arab envoys Hanzuo, Yanji, and Shabei were all appointed gentlemen of the palace and sent home.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：西方之國，綿亙山川，自張騫奉使已來，介子立功之後，通於中國者多矣。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: The historian remarks: The states of the west stretch across mountains and rivers; from the time Zhang Qian was sent on mission, and after Jiezi won merit, many have had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The western lands stretch across mountains and rivers. Since Zhang Qian's mission and after Jiezi earned his merit, countless peoples have opened ties with China.

sentences.zh: 有唐拓境，遠極安西，弱者德以懷之，強者力以制之。

translations.literal: The Tang expanded its borders, reaching far to Anxi; the weak were embraced with virtue, the strong were controlled with force.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang pushed its frontiers to distant Anxi, winning the weak with virtue and restraining the strong with force.

sentences.zh: 開元之前，貢輸不絕。

translations.literal: Before the Kaiyuan era, tribute and deliveries never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Kaiyuan era, tribute flowed without interruption.

sentences.zh: 天寶之亂，邊僥多虞，邠郊之西，即為戎狄，槁街之邸，來朝亦稀。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Tianbao the frontier was full of alarms; west of Bin and the suburbs lay the Rong and Di; at the lodges of Gaojie, those coming to court were also few.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianbao rebellion brought constant frontier alarms; west of Bin the land passed to the barbarians, and envoys at the guest lodges of the capital grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 故古先哲王，務寧華夏，語曰：「近者悅，遠者來。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity strove to bring peace to Huaxia; it is said: "When those near are pleased, those far will come."
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old sought peace for the Central Realm, as the saying runs: "When those nearby are content, those afar will come."

sentences.zh: 斯之謂矣！

translations.literal: This is what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: So the proverb teaches.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：大蒙之人，西方之國，與時盛衰，隨世通塞。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The people of great Meng, the states of the west, rise and fall with the times, open and close with the age.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The peoples of the far west rise and fall with the times, their roads to China opening or closing as fortune allows.

sentences.zh: 勿謂戎心，不懷我德；

translations.literal: Do not suppose the hearts of the Rong do not cherish our virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Do not imagine that barbarian hearts are deaf to our virtue;

sentences.zh: 貞觀、開元，槁街充斥。

translations.literal: in the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, Gaojie was thronged.
translations.idiomatic: under Zhenguan and Kaiyuan the guest lodges overflowed with envoys.
